crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
本綱要僅供選課參考，正式授課大綱將於開學第一週於課堂中公布。

Motion Capture (MoCap) plays a crucial role in various Virtual Reality and Metaverse applications. In this course, we discuss how MoCap technology tracks and records users movements, such as hand tracking, full-body tracking, eye tracking, and face tracking. The course is designed for beginners, explaining the basics of motion capture, including hardware and software. These concepts can be applied in future Virtual and Augmented Reality-mediated communication, such as user-driven avatars, bringing our creative visions of future human-computer interaction to life.

動作捕捉在各種虛擬實境和元宇宙應用扮演關鍵角色。在這門課，我們討論如何透過動作捕捉技術追蹤和紀錄使用者的各種動作，例如手部追蹤、全身追蹤、眼球和表情追蹤，本課程是為初學者設計，講解動作捕捉基礎知識，包括硬體和軟體內容。這些概念可以應用於未來虛擬和擴增實境中介傳播，例如使用者動作即時呈現的虛擬化身，將我們對未來人機互動的創意願景變為現實。

課程探討混合實境及虛擬實境之構築元素，強調3D虛擬世界之視覺意象及美感技法，試圖創造獨特奇幻之視覺美術風格，進而強化虛構非實境之沈浸感體驗及想像維度。

課程技術層面結合高斯潑濺(3DGS)、AI coding assistant (Github Copilot)、AI生成模型、3D素材庫進行三維空間場景設計，並以遊戲引擎Unreal Engine或TouchDesigner為開發工具進行場景運鏡體驗與互動設計。理論層面，則以李飛飛教授之空間智慧(Spatial Intelligence)，及經典戲劇理論，例如布魯克《空的空間》作為討論框架，試圖探索在AI生成世界下人類的嶄新空間感知，以及在虛擬世界增強群體共感經驗。

實作三大主軸，(ㄧ) 結合Marble AI, Luma AI, Apple Sharp AI, TripoSplat AI 進行虛擬場景設計。(二) 以3DGS為出發輔以Github Copilot，進行風格化場景設計(non-photorealistic scenic design)及視覺特效(post-process effect：Bloom、Filmic Tonemaping、Color grading、Vignette、Depth of field、Lens Flare...)等等表現技法提升美術質地。(三) 加上模擬機制、氣候狀態、運鏡與互動等。

crs_outline:
本課程主要在研讀與探究幽靈敘事理論，釐清「集體無意識」、「文化無意識」(歷史記憶的區域)，以及「外顯的文化模式」之間的關聯性，以及文化創傷的代際傳遞過程及其產生的影響。課程目標包括以下：
1.	將「幽靈敘事」所討論的相關潛影轉化為可見可聞可理解的文本或行動，並將相關知識對應到個人世界、所屬團體、家族社會或國家。
2.	對發生中或曾發生過的創傷暴力事件，進行反思批判，建構有意義的對話，以作爲朝向未來的借鏡。
3.	激發學生以多元的知識或藝術生產方式來顯影幽靈記憶。

crs_outline:
「科學是否讓我們得以感知世界的神聖？還是它以某種方式扭曲了光線，反而遮蔽了這份神聖？」
——羅賓·沃爾·金默勒（Robin Wall Kimmerer）《Braiding Sweetgrass》

本課以「超寫生」作為核心教學法，每一堂課都會是一個以非視覺感官為主的寫生工作室。每一堂課將引入一個「模特/寫生物件」（可能是一個物件、一段聲音、一種氣味、一個動作、一個時間系統）。同學需要在課堂時間內完成一個「轉譯」，用視覺以外的方式（觸覺、聽覺、嗅覺、味覺、溫度、濕度、節奏、壓力）把它變成可被他人讀到的作品。我們學習透過視覺之外的多重感官來「觀察」世界。

課程同時引入非線性敘事與多重時間概念：我們將練習把「時間」當成材料來構思，而不是把作品塞進過去>現在>未來的單一路徑。我們學習運用非線性時間「構思」創作。

透過閱讀、工作坊、以及每週快速產出的寫生原型，同學會逐步建立自己的「感官方法」與「非線性構思語法」。這堂課藉由擺脫既有框架的限制，讓設計想像在感官與時序的交錯中重組，產生新的知識與觀點。

cos_cname: 質疑性設計：動力互動藝術協作實踐
memo: (不受理紙本加簽, 校際選修除外) 應藝所優先（同時開放大三、大四、電機／建築相關系所學生選修）
cos_ename: Interrogative Design: Collaborative Practices of Kinetic Interactive Art
crs_outline:
一、課程概述
本課以動力互動藝術為創作主軸，透過動力雕塑、機構裝置與互動科技的技術實作，建立學生對「動態」與「互動」在藝術中的基礎理解，並導入科學方法與實作為研究的思維，將創作過程視為假設、實驗、觀察與迭代的結構化循環。 在此脈絡中，科技同時被視為具物質限制的材料、行為系統的結構，以及具社會意涵的論述媒介，支持學生在作品中有意識地設計運動語彙、互動邏輯與觀眾體驗。

同時，本課以新竹六燃園區的歷史與現況作為主要場域與議題脈絡，結合質疑性設計觀念，將設計與藝術創作視為「生成公共問句」的途徑。 學生將從六燃作為戰爭燃料廠、眷村聚落及今日科技城市節點的多重身分出發，研究無法被簡化或輕易解決的結構性問題，例如戰爭與能源、記憶與遺址、科技發展與地方不平等等，並透過動力互動裝置在公共或半公共空間中製造可見的衝突場景與討論場域。

課程特別強調跨領域團隊協作：藝術、設計、工程、建築等不同背景的學生將在混合小組中工作，練習將科學方法導入創作流程。

二、課程目標
修課學生預期能在課程結束時達成以下目標：

1.技術與科學方法：以結構化實驗支持動力互動創作
能操作基本機構設計（連桿、齒輪、凸輪等）與光互動系統（感測與控制），並以科學方法規劃原型實驗與迭代。
2.理解新媒體與動力互動藝術的理論基礎理解新媒體藝術、動力藝術與資訊體驗設計的核心概念，包含科技作為材料／系統／論述的三重角色，以及互動性、參與觀眾與公共空間的關係。
3.掌握質疑性設計的思考方法
能說明質疑性設計與一般設計思考、批判設計、社會實踐藝術之差異，理解「以問題為成果」的取向，並在創作中處理公共性、衝突性與參與社群的倫理議題。
4.以六燃場域為核心提出公共問句
透過六燃實地踏查、文件閱讀與訪談，辨識與戰爭、能源、記憶、科技城市相關的結構性問題，並將這些問題轉化為具空間與行為感的「公共問句」，作為作品主軸。
5.在跨域團隊中協作並理解組織管理邏輯與挑戰
能在混合背景的團隊中進行角色分工與溝通，辨識專業語言差異與權力不對稱，透過協作日誌與期末報告分析團隊決策過程，並將這些經驗視為作品的一部分，而非背景噪音。

設計與實現一件以「質疑性設計」為核心的動力互動作品：
完成一件以六燃相關公共問句為核心的動力互動裝置，能在展出中清楚讓觀眾「被問題攤開」，而非提供單一解答，並在口頭報告與書面文件中反思作品的技術選擇、場域關係與倫理考量。

crs_outline: 「跨媒介視覺設計」為視覺設計面對跨領域的研討課程，基於「媒介即訊息」的觀點，設計工作者要處理的不只是內容本身，而是巧用媒介，更深刻地塑造思維、創造文化與掌握他人的行動方式。媒介可以是任何形式的傳播工具，例如口語表達、文字符號、繪畫與影像、印刷媒體、電子媒體、社交媒體平台等。跨媒介的呈現的對於受眾來說極度重要，也同時影響創作者在對於設計的各種轉化與表述的功力。對此時代的設計工作者，若缺乏了正視媒介的視野，他們的作品將難以與世界真正對話。本課程提供設計相關工作者必備的鑑賞能力，通透的識讀任何媒介，無論是對語言、文字、圖像、影片，乃至社群、互動裝置、影音平台，都可以洞見其隱含的特定語法與權力關係，在此基礎上，將知識導入設計工作與作品之中。

crs_outline:
大眾對於醫療品質的追求一直是各種先進技術導入醫療場域的強烈動機來源，其中，3D掃瞄設備技術在近年快速普及，使得人體體表逆向掃瞄變得更加容易實現，這種非接觸式且精準地建構人體數位模型的光學技術逐漸被討論用來替代傳統醫療製作各類穿戴式輔具、護具、矯正器的實體翻模方法。而同樣也在快速普及的3D列印由於近年來成本降低、品質提昇、效率加快，也逐漸被討論到用來進行客製化醫療用品或少量製造產品的可能性，使得原本因無法達到生產經濟規模門檻的產品得到落實的可能。

基於上述背景，本課程由兩個產品設計開發單元構成，第一單元為應用人體3D掃瞄與3D列印進行 Patient-Matched Device 客製化穿戴裝置之製作，第二單位為針對需求量少的診斷或復健用品進行以 3D列印及少量製造為前提的設計開發。

第一單元Patient-Matched Device 客製化穿戴裝置之設計製作，將教授學生針對身體特定部位，如頭、四肢、軀幹來設計客製化之穿戴裝置，課程中將運用手持式3D掃瞄器對所設定之身體局部進得體表網格模型，並運用教師提供之程式來生成可穿戴的鏤空薄殻結構，最終運用3D列印將之實體。課程中，學生將習得此一數位化工作流程並發掘可能潛在問題。

第二單元分為兩個主題A、B，主題A延續學生在第一單元所製作的客製化穿戴薄殻作為載體，由於此載體長時間配戴於使用者身上，因此獲得貼近其身體收集生理或環境數據的可能，例如偵測皮膚腫脹壓力、局部體表溫濕度、肢體活動彎曲角度等、所處環境空氣品質等等，其偵測不一定為醫療目的，可以延伸為推測設計或互動藝術創作之面向。因此學生可依據其設計目的來選擇適用的偵測元件，在載體作植入元件設計，並驗證是否滿足其預期目的、收集數據或觸發互動之可行性。主題B則為針對治療復健過程中使用之產品的IOT與3D列印化設計，這些產品中有些會用來幫助治療師判斷患者手、脚、眼、腦的活動效率，例如三分鐘登階測試或單手及手指靈活度評估測試器材，由於這些產品的市場需求量少，製造商缺乏開發生產意願，因此通常以簡易、低成本器材型態為主。然而這些產品具有收集大數據之潛力，因此主題B為透過電子元件與Arduino將這些產品轉化為自動化且能收集第一手數據的原型設計，並以 3D列印思維克服量產門檻。

memo: (不受理紙本加簽, 校際選修除外) 應藝所優先；上課教室：人二館教學工場 HB13
cos_ename: Digital Technology in Ceramic Fabrication and Creative Practice
crs_outline:
本課程以陶瓷材料為主，透過陶土與釉藥作為主要材料，並以科技輔助陶藝創作為核心概念進行教學。課程目標除了讓同學理解傳統陶瓷製作方式，如手捏、拉坯成型，以及工業化生產中常見的石膏灌漿與旋坯等工法之外，也進一步引導同學認識如何運用數位科技工具輔助陶藝創作與製造流程。

相較於傳統陶瓷在打樣或量產時，往往需要經歷開模製作與反覆溝通修正等繁複程序，科技工具的介入能夠有效縮短製作流程，並快速建立多樣化的作品形式與可能性。本課程旨在使修課同學理解科技輔助製造在陶藝創作與製造上的便利性，並藉此拓展對陶瓷創作方法的手段，期待激發更多跨越傳統製程的創作可能性。

課程分成以下幾個單元：
第一單元：雷射切割與陶盤製造
透過 Grasshopper 進行紋理與圖樣設計，並運用雷射切割技術製作模具，完成陶盤的製作流程，理解數位設計如何轉換為實體陶瓷作品。
第二單元：CNC 銑床與花磚製造
使用 Grasshopper 建立數位模型，並透過電腦數值控制（CNC）銑床進行加工，製作具客製化特徵的陶瓷花磚，認識數位製造於陶瓷產製中的應用方式。
第三單元：3D 列印與馬克杯製造
利用 Grasshopper 設計表面肌理，透過陶瓷 3D 列印技術製作杯體。同時結合石膏模具灌漿方式製作杯把，使同學理解數位製造與傳統陶瓷產業製程之間的整合與應用。

costype: 基本素養-生命及品格教育
crs_outline:
課程介紹：人之為人 (Being Human) —— 從生物載體到覺醒的自然人
一、 課程主題：重構「人」的完整性
在當代高等教育中，「人」往往被拆解為不同學科下的功能碎片。在生物學中，我們被視為精密的生化機器；在社會學中，我們是階級與體制下的角色；在資訊科學中，我們則成了一串可預測的數據。然而，在這些碎片化的知識背後，那個關於「我是誰」的終極追問卻往往被遺忘了。本課程旨在重構那份失落的「完整人類經驗」，帶領大家穿透「生物人」的物質智慧、認清「社會人」的故事枷鎖，最終尋回那個與宇宙天地共振的「自然人」本體。
二、 課程理念：在存在中遇見知曉
我們對世界的認識，往往受限於我們當下的狀態。本課程的核心理念在於打破「知識僅是資訊累積」的迷思，轉而探討一種「存在即知曉」（Being as Knowing）的可能性。
借用赫胥黎（Aldous Huxley）與西方神祕主義的洞見：一個人的認知深度，其實是他生命品質的函數。這意味著，當我們的心靈處於機械式的反應與混濁的睡眠中時，有些真相是無論讀多少書都無法觸碰的。因此，我們在課程中提倡一種「證悟」高於「解悟」的態度——解悟是研讀地圖，而證悟則是腳步的抵達。我們將練習一種「感知領悟」（Sense of Knowing），這不是枯燥的邏輯推演，而是一種全方位的直覺性領會。當我們試著提升自己的「存在狀態」，讓內在變得更清澈透明時，那些關於生命的終極答案，便會像水面下的礁石在潮退後顯現一樣，自然地從你的生命中彰顯出來。
三、 課程路徑：四個階段的生命實驗
1. 發現機械性（W2-W7）： 旅程從我們最親近的身體出發。我們將驚嘆於細胞間極致的合作智慧，並以此為鏡，透過哈拉瑞（Yuval Noah Harari）與薩波斯基（Robert Sapolsky）的視野，誠實地觀察自己如何被社會故事與生理本能所驅動。這是一個「覺察」的過程，練習在日常中認出那些「機械式睡眠」的時刻。
2. 普世智慧與轉向（W9-W11）： 接著，我們將跨越東西方，進入「長青哲學」與神祕主義的世界。這是一個向內尋找導航系統的階段，我們將嘗試透過審美直觀與良知，去感受那個超越感官、與宇宙本源相契合的時刻。這不是要學習新教條，而是要驗證那些古老智慧在當代生活中的真實性。
3. 多維整合與探索（W12-W14）： 以榮格（Carl Gustav Jung）學說與唯識學建立超越個體的意識模型後，我們將結合肯·威爾伯（Ken Wilber）的意識階梯與賽斯（Seth material）的多維實相論。我們將探討意識如何像光線一樣投影出我們所見的物質世界，並學習識別那些隱藏在生活細節中的「共時性」提示，理解生命在垂直演化與水平擴張間的壯闊景致。
4. 歸於終極自由（W15）： 旅程的終點，是關於「放下」。我們將實踐萊斯特·利文森（Lester Levenson）的釋放法，剝離那些我們自願承擔的限制與重擔。最終的目標並非獲得更多，而是回歸一種「成為你之所是」的純粹喜悅。
四、 結語：邀請你，成為知曉本身
「人之為人」不提供標準答案，而是提供一套邀請。我們希望這門課結束時，你帶走的不是一張寫滿筆記的紙，而是一個更敏銳、更有存在感的靈魂。當你提升了「存在」的品質，你本身就是那份知曉真理的容器。

crs_outline:
This course will introduce students to crucial theories in gender and sexuality studies. The course will start with classical texts and then proceed to contemporary theories in the field. In addition to theory, we will also read films, moving-image works, digital media arts, scripts of avant-garde and underground performances, memoirs or “biomythography,” and activist video works so that students can understand that the discipline of gender and sexuality studies is never born out of the interests of researchers in the ivory tower. Instead, it is a field where scholars “do theory” with social commitments and utopian aspirations for social change while enduring social and political oppression and, in the meantime, creating new forms of socialities and relationalities. 
---
做為一個由被壓迫者集結與形塑而成的學術領域，性別研究一直是一個與當前社會脈絡與文化政治緊密勾連的學科。本課程以此作為立足點與出發點，向學生引介性別研究裡的重要理論與議題。課程會由較為古典的性別理論開始，之後進行至當代重要的理論與議題。除了閱讀理論，我們也會討論電影與動態影像作品、數位電影/藝術、前衛與地下表演劇本、回憶錄或自傳神話、以及藝術家和社會運動行動者的抗議性影像藝術或行為藝術等。如此，修課學生將會理解性別研究從來就不是象牙塔裡的追尋，也與流行、商品化或「認同政治」等學術污名或窄化定義無關。相反的，它一直是一個受壓迫者為了求生存而集結與誕生的學術領域，也一直在不斷變動與更新的壓迫性環境裡思索與記憶少數群體的歷史與政治創傷，並同時形塑新型態的社會關係與社群。

cos_cname: 島嶼東亞：帝國、身體、空間政治
memo: [English Medium Course]
cos_ename: Archipelagic East Asia: Empire, Body, and Spatial Politics
dep_ename: Institute for Social Research and Cultural Studies
crs_outline:
This course explores the making of modern East Asia through the lenses of critical historiographical turns, archipelagic thinking, and the politics of embodiment. Moving beyond nation-centered narratives, the course examines how empire, colonial modernity, and shifting spatial imaginaries shaped lived experiences across Taiwan, Japan/Okinawa, Korean Peninsula, Hong Kong, and the wider Pacific world.
This course consists of three sections: (1)Archipelagic Turn, (2) Bodies under Empire (3) Spatializing East Asia. We begin by situating postwar intellectual transformations within the broader “cultural turn” in historical studies, drawing on Geoff Eley and debates on colonial modernity. The course then develops an “Archipelagic Turn,” engaging with the Black Atlantic, Pacific Rim discourses, and critiques of area studies to reconsider East Asia as a fluid, interconnected space rather than a fixed geopolitical entity.
The second section “Bodies under Empire” investigates how imperial power operated through hunger, health, reproduction, and racialization. Topics include starvation science and geopolitics, eugenics and total war, colonial governance in Taiwan and Hong Kong, and the Okinawan experience of the “Cycad Hell.” Here, the body becomes a crucial site where empire materializes through regulation, deprivation, and survival.
The final section “Spatializing East Asia” brings the course into direct dialogue with its central themes of empire, body, and spatial politics. Rather than treating war as a discrete event, this section examines how imperial power reorganizes space—through caves, camps, and infrastructures of confinement—and how these spaces, in turn, shape embodied experience. From the caves (gama) of Okinawa to prisoner-of-war camps in Southeast Asia, we explore how landscapes become technologies of survival, coercion, and memory. Engaging with the idea of a “liquid” East Asia, the course ultimately approaches the region not as a fixed geopolitical container but as an archipelagic formation—an interconnected yet fractured field shaped by imperial mobility, displacement, and contested spatial orders. By tracing the entanglement of bodies and spaces under empire, this course invites students to rethink East Asia as a dynamic configuration of power, movement, and lived experience.
本課程以批判史學轉向、群島思維與身體政治為線索，探討現代東亞在帝國與戰爭條件下的歷史構成。課程超越國族中心敘事，檢視殖民現代性與空間想像如何形塑台灣、日本/沖繩、朝鮮半島、香港及太平洋區域的歷史經驗。第一單元「群島轉向」以文化轉向與殖民現代性辯論為起點，透過 Geoff Eley、Tani Barlow 與 Arif Dirlik 的討論，反思「區域」概念的形成與限制。在此基礎上本課程建立「群島轉向」的視角，將東亞理解為流動且相互連結的知識生產與權力空間，而非固定的地理框架。
第二單元「帝國下的身體」探討帝國權力如何透過飢餓、健康、生殖與種族化等機制運作。議題包括飢餓科學與地緣政治、優生學與總動員戰爭、台港殖民治理，以及沖繩「蘇鐵地獄」所反映的身體、種族及治理議題；探究身體如何成為帝國支配與動員的核心場域。
第三單元「空間化東亞」關注東亞政治的地景與秩序，分析戰爭時期至戰後亞洲的權力地景如何在洞窟、「營」與拘禁場所中重組。從沖繩戰的gama (ガマ)到台灣、東南亞的戰俘營，本單元探討空間如何成為壓迫、生存與歷史記憶共存的場所。透過「液態東亞」的視角，本課程最後將「東亞」延伸為一種群島式的空間政治線索，提供探索當代知識生產與權力形構的新視野。

crs_outline:
從圍堵與禁制的高牆，到如影隨形的數位監控；從安全、平等與權利的屏障，到團結抵抗的前提；從認同與差異、包容與排除的界線，到多樣生命形式混雜交錯的空間……
什麼是邊界？邊界在哪裡？為何設立邊界？邊界如何作用？誰是邊界行動者？有哪些不同的邊界體驗？
在當代世界中，隨著邊界型態、技術、功能與行動者不斷演變與擴充，對於移動的調控也愈加複雜、隱微，甚至難以察覺。本課程將結合跨領域的理論文獻、案例分析與實地踏查，透過邊界及其相關概念，探討各種虛實交錯的邊界工法如何成為當代世界權力運作的重要機制與場域；同時，形形色色的人與非人的移動，又如何順應、迴避、鬆動、僭越既有的邊界結構，並引發新的邊界實踐。

Independent Study aims to help students prepare their own thesis/dissertation projects or develop specific areas of research.Please e-mail me at the beginning of the semester (ie. first week) to introduce yourself, discuss your reading list or target archive, and arrange our individual meeting schedule. We can meet once a month, two to three times each semester, depending on your progress. Before each meeting (ie. at least two days ahead), please send me your reading note, field note, or response paper regarding the materials you work on. I particularly welcome those who plan to work on media and film studies, architecture/city/infrastructure critique, war/military history, environmental/ecological criticism, or modern literature and visual cultures.


個別研究意在協助碩博班同學發展個別化閱讀書單，探索特定研究領域，以便進行各階段論文寫作。有意進行個別研究的同學請於開學前與我聯繫，以便安排該學期會面時間及確定閱讀/寫作進度。原則上，我建議每學期會面2-3次。請於學期初與我討論、擬定閱讀書單或欲調查之文獻檔案，並於每次會面2天前將閱讀或調查筆記以電子郵件寄給我。歡迎對媒介理論、電影研究、建築與城市研究文化遺就 、戰爭文化史、生態敘事與影像、近現代比較文學與報刊文化等領域有興趣的同學與我進行個別研究。

課程概述與目標：
This course provides graduate students with comprehensive training in research methodologies, emphasizing practical application of diverse research methods while engaging with contemporary debates about methodological innovation in critical humanities and social sciences. Students will develop skills in research design, data collection, analysis, and delivery while critically examining how methodological decisions are political and shape knowledge production.

The course is organized into three main units: The first part, Foundations of Cultural Studies Research, introduces students to epistemological debates within cultural studies, examining how the field’s interdisciplinary tendency demands reflexive research practices and methodological innovation. The second part, Qualitative Research Methods and Practices, provides hands-on training in ethnographic fieldwork, interview techniques, discourse analysis, archival research, and digital methods for studying historical and current cultural formations. The third unit, Contemporary Challenges and Innovations, addresses emerging methodological approaches including digital ethnography, multimodal analysis, participatory research methods, and ethical considerations in cultural research.

Students will engage with both established and new methodological approaches, developing critical perspectives on how to select, adapt, and combine research methods appropriate to their specific research questions and contexts. The course emphasizes reflexive practice, encouraging students to examine their own positionality as researchers while developing practical skills in research design, data analysis, and scholarly communication.

crs_outline:
本課程為文化研究之入門概論，以「人民／民眾／大眾」為核心主題，引領學生認識文化研究的主要理論取向與分析方法。「大眾」既是現代政治動員的對象、文化生產的受眾，也是媒介中介的主體，其概念本身即折射出文化研究跨學科、多向度的知識關懷。本課程藉由聚焦這一主題，帶領學生掌握文化研究的問題意識與核心論爭。
課程分三個單元展開。第一單元「諸民之辨」從政治哲學切入，辨析「人民」概念在現代語境中的多重形態——從無民到民粹，從民族自決到社會運動——揭示「民」作為政治主體的內在張力與歷史變遷。第二單元轉向文化史與文化社會學，透過Burke、Adorno、Bourdieu、Gramsci等人的經典文本，考察大眾文化如何在與精英文化的對立中被定義，如何成為霸權競逐的場域，以及如何在新自由主義治理下重塑主體性。第三單元「Mediating the Mass」則引入媒介理論，從海德格、班雅明、克拉考爾到霍爾、麥克魯漢、基特勒，探討媒介如何構成大眾感知與認同的基礎設施，並延伸至當代平台文化與粉絲經濟的討論。
三個單元雖各有理論重心，卻共享一個問題意識：面對「人民／民眾／大眾」這一充滿爭議的概念，文化研究如何以跨學科的視野，揭示其中複雜交織的權力關係、文化實踐與認同政治。修習本課程，學生將獲得進入文化研究領域的基本理論裝備與批判性閱讀能力。

crs_outline:
Course Description (For English version, please scroll down)

本課程從媒介研究的角度從新審視「環境」此一概念，並探問三個相互纏繞的問題：(1) 媒介如何再現自然/人造環境，形塑我們的理解與感知 (2) 作為技術系統或基礎設施的媒介如何成為人類環境的一部分。(3) 關於環境的思考如何開啟重思當代媒介理論的方法。 從礦物、大氣、海洋、動物、昆蟲、病毒，我們將閱讀並思考當代媒介思想家如何試圖超越人類中心的媒介論，將被隱蔽的自然環境與非人他者重新納入論述視野。另一方面，從高空攝影、網路監視、虛擬遊戲、平台經濟、都市基礎設施等具體案例，我們將思考人類如何透過媒介技術重新「創造世界」(world-making) 或形塑「第二自然」(second nature)。我們亦將進一步探問，在媒介/環境的雙重糾纏中，性別、階級、族裔等認同與地緣政治類別又如何被區分成「自然」或「異類」。本課程閱讀及討論語言以英文為主，中文為輔，並搭配電影、小說文本、攝影圖像等媒介類型分析。課堂討論外，兩週一次閱讀筆記、一份期末報告、學期中另有2場邀請演講需出席。

This course asks the following questions: (1) how is environment represented in multiple forms and genres of media? (2) how do media—as technical system and infrastructure—become part of our environment and second nature? (3) how does the notion of environment redefine media and media theory? These questions will guide us through the classical elements of water, air, fire, earth, as well as the species and strains of animals, insects, and viruses . Through fictions, films, photographs, video games, and digital platforms, we will explore the ways human beings imagine natural and artificial environments and inquire into a series of ideas about the environment conveyed through the imagined landscapes of oceans, rivers, mountains, farmlands, as well as the human-built infrastructure and architecture. The media/environment complex tells us more than about how we imagine nature and the environment. They articulate and naturalize ideas about race, gender, class, geopolitics, and the very boundary between the human and the non-human. They present certain kinds of identities as natural and normative and other kinds of identities as unnatural or out of place in nature. We will explore the ways that representations of environment can at times justify existing relationships of power and the ways in which such representations may also contest the status quo. As part of this class, you will be responsible for contributing examples of environmental media to class discussion through your response papers. One of the aims of the seminar is to help you critically engage with both the medium-specificity and site-specificity of environments.

crs_outline:
本課程以「經典、品味與權力」為題，從文化研究的視角探討文學與藝術如何被生產、命名、區分、消費與爭奪。課程關注的不只是作品本身，而是作品如何在特定的社會關係、制度安排與歷史脈絡中取得意義與價值。我們將討論：什麼能被稱為經典？誰有資格定義品味？文化價值如何與階級、性別、教育、市場、媒介與權力結構交織？課程將結合理論閱讀與具體案例，處理作者、觀眾、文化資本、經典形成、展示制度、文化工業，以及數位平台等議題，並思考文學與藝術如何不只是再現社會，也參與建構社會現實。透過跨越文學研究、藝術社會學、文化理論與文化政治的討論，本課程旨在引導學生理解文化價值從來不是自然存在，而是在不斷的分類、鬥爭與協商中被形塑。課程特別適合對文化研究、文學、藝術、社會理論與當代文化政治有興趣的研究生。
課程目標
修課完成後，學生應能：
理解文學與藝術研究中的主要社會理論問題與爭議。
辨識不同理論傳統對作品、作者、價值、制度與觀眾的不同理解。
以社會理論語彙分析具體的文學或藝術現象。
建立比較不同理論立場的能力，而非只停留在作者或概念羅列。

dep_cname: 亞際文化研究國際碩士學位學程（台灣聯合大學系統）
dep_ename: International Master's Program in Inter-Asia Cultural Studies (University System of Taiwan)
crs_outline:
主旨

冷戰結束後曾出現短暫的「民主擴張期」，然而進入二十一世紀以來，全球政治逐漸呈現出明顯的專制回潮與民主倒退。這一現象不再僅限於少數非民主國家，而是以不同形式出現在多種制度環境之中：從東歐與中亞的選舉型威權政體，到中東與拉丁美洲的安全化治理，再到亞洲高度制度化的國家治理體系，專制傾向逐漸透過法律、行政、科技與敘事策略嵌入日常治理之中。即使在原本被視為制度成熟的民主國家，例如美國在川普政府時期所呈現的政治實踐，也顯示出某些專制治理技術可以在民主制度內部逐步浮現。
本課程將延續本人最新著作，Tianxia and Its Discontents: Confucian Political Theology, Coloniality, and the Global Order (Routledge 2026)，從跨學科的理論視角繼續深入探討天下治理背後的慾望。本課程的核心假設是：專制並不僅僅是一種政體分類，而是一種政治慾望與治理邏輯。在社會不安、經濟轉型與地緣政治競爭加劇的條件下，社會與政治精英之間可能逐漸形成對秩序、集中權力與全面治理的需求，這種需求構成了本文所稱的專制慾望。當這種慾望與特定的行政技術、法律機制與治理工具結合時，便可能形成一套跨制度運作的治理模式。
在歷史層面，本課程將回溯中國帝制特別是盛清時期所發展的專制治理模式。透過人口治理、思想控制、邊疆管理與官僚行政體系等制度，帝國政權建立了一套高度集中且制度化的治理技術，使中央權力得以管理廣大疆域與多樣人口。這些歷史治理技術構成理解當代治理轉型的重要參照。
在當代層面，本課程將進一步分析數位基礎設施如何改寫治理技術。資料系統、演算法治理、人工智慧與全球數位網絡，使得人口監測、資訊整合與行政管理的能力大幅提升。這些技術並不必然導致專制體制，但它們顯著擴大了專制慾望得以實現的技術條件。透過對中國數位絲路與全球數位基礎設施擴張的案例分析，本課程將探討一個更宏觀的問題：當專制慾望、治理技術與數位基礎設施相互交織時，是否正在形成一種新的全球治理形態——本人稱之為數位天下（Digital Tianxia）。
本課程因此嘗試從政治理論、歷史制度與科技基礎設施三個層面，重新思考二十一世紀權力運作的方式，以及專制治理在數位時代的可能轉型。
本門課要探討以下問題：
核心議題：
為何21世紀出現了大量專制治理的傾向？我們如何從美國川普政府分析其專制化治理特性？匈牙利、俄國、土耳其、伊朗、中亞國家、中國及其他威權體制國家有什麼共性？
如何理解專制？目前對於專制體制的研究是否能夠讓我們思考專制治理的模式？例如Hanna Arendt (1968) The Origins of Totalitarianism，Theodor W. Adorno (1969) The Authoritarian Personality，Levitsky ＆amp;amp; Ziblatt（2018） How Democracies Die，Milan W. Svolik（2012, 2019）The Politics of Authoritarian Rule，Anne Applebaum（2020）Twilight of Democracy，以及其他大量快速增加的研究，能否解釋專制治理背後的慾望？
中國帝制如何執行其專制治理的模式？我們將從五個模組來討論中國帝制的專制治理技術：人口治理、思想治理、邊疆治理、官商貪腐的資本集中、行政擴張的域外管轄。這些治理技術如何以傅柯的《安全、領土、人口》來理解？
中國21世紀的數位絲路如何展現了其專制慾望？我們要探討數位絲路、演算法以及AI如何刺激並增強了專制慾望，並完善了其專制治理技術。傅柯的《安全、領土、人口》如何在數位時代被改寫？
每週討論問題（Discussion Questions）

Week 1｜導論  專制回潮與數位天下
數位基礎設施是否正在重組全球治理秩序？
「數位天下」是否可以成為理解二十一世紀權力的新概念？

Week 2｜數位絲路與全球基礎設施
中國一帶一路以及數位絲路的數位基礎設施如何成為地緣政治工具？
技術標準與網路基礎設施如何擴展國家影響力？

Week 3｜中國帝制治理：人口與行政
中國帝制如何管理龐大人口與廣大疆域？
戶籍制度與官僚行政體系如何形成治理網絡？

Week 4｜盛清時期的思想治理與文化控制
帝國政權如何透過思想與知識管理維持統治？
文化與知識制度在治理中扮演何種角色？

Week 5｜邊疆治理與帝國秩序
歷代帝國如何管理邊疆民族與多元疆域？
盛清時期如何大幅擴張領土？邊疆治理如何影響帝國的政治想像？

Week 6｜治理性
傅柯的《安全、領土、人口》如何協助我們理解現代國家透過治理術管理人口與社會的技術？
治理術如何改變我們理解權力的方式？

Week 7｜為何二十一世紀出現「專制回潮」的全球趨勢？
民主制度內部如何可能出現專制治理傾向？

Week 8｜競爭式威權政體與民主制度下的專制治理
「威權體制」與「專制治理」在理論上有何差異？
將專制理解為治理技術而非政體分類，會帶來什麼新的分析視角？如何理解民主制度下出現的專制治理模式？

Week 9｜專制慾望的政治心理
社會在何種條件下會產生對集中權力與秩序的需求？
專制慾望如何在政治敘事與民粹動員中被激發？

Week 10｜民主制度下民粹主義與專制治理的關聯
民主制度如何可能逐步出現「專制化」的治理模式？
美國川普政府的治理實踐可以如何理解？

Week 11｜演算法治理術
演算法如何改變了知識與權力的關係？
演算法如何透過數據模式操作其治理術？
Week 12｜監視體系與資本權力
數位官僚體系與監視系統之間如何互動？
行政權力與資本集中之間有何關係？

Week 13｜物流部署與基礎建設
物流、數據、平台與演算法如何改變治理方式？
基礎建設如何創造新的權力形態？

Week 14｜AI、數據殖民治理技術
數據提取如何促成了新型態的殖民治理模式？
人工智慧如何影響國家治理與社會控制？是否加強專制治理能力？

Week 15｜期末報告

crs_outline:
Content: This course attempts to develop certain perspectives with regard to the sociocultural study of the modern nation-state while at the same time noting their ramifications for a reassessment of prevailing concepts of ethnicity and identity and suggesting possible avenues for future empirical research.  Both nationalism and the state have been intense topics of discussion in the social scientific literature.  While interdisciplinary in approach, this course intends to focus mainly on the cultural and ethnic dimensions of the nation-state rather than its politico-institutional features per se, insofar as the latter impinges on the former.  It will also be historically sensitive and cross-cultural in scope, as a means of differentiating the generalities and specificities of nation-state formation.  Due to the expanding nature of the literature, it may be necessary to substitute newer readings and topics as they become available and relevant.
Format: The first week will be devoted to an overview of the problematic followed by a description of subsequent topics of discussion.  Each topic will roughly cover a week's work, although this may in practice vary according to the respective length and density of the readings themselves.  This will leave about four weeks for oral presentation of research papers.  Presentations may take any of these forms: a) literature review of a specialized topic of interest or b) detailed, critical commentary on a monograph not explicitly discussed in class lectures.  Oral presentations should ideally serve as proposals or outlines for a larger term paper to be turned in at the conclusion of the course.  The first half of each class session will be devoted to a short presentation by the lecturer and followed by open discussion.  The class lecture will revolve closely around assigned syllabus readings.  I expect also that people will participate actively in class discussions by referring to recommended and other related readings to supplement and challenge points already raised.  Oral and written performance will thus contribute to the overall course marks.

課程概述
建築結構系統包含”結構系統”與”結構學”兩大內涵，是建築設計的基礎，也是各類建築國家考試必考之科目。完整的教學規畫須透過”建築結構系統(I)(II)”(分為兩學期，各為3學分)來闡述。
(A) "建築結構系統(I)”課程主要內容與目標 :
◎各類型結構系統與結構行為
包括框架、桁架、拱、板殼、薄膜、懸索、木造、磚石造、   RC造、鋼骨造及各類型建築物基礎之構成。
◎鋼筋混凝土與鋼骨結構設計基本概念與設計研判。
◎抗震結構、抗風結構、隔震消能結構。
◎結構系統與建築規劃設計之整合。
(B) "建築結構系統(II)”課程主要內容與目標 :
◎基本結構力學原理
◎結構力學與構件設計及結構行為之關聯性
◎與時事有關之建築結構問題。
課程目標
”建築結構系統(I)”課程主要課程目標 :
◎瞭解各類型結構系統與結構行為。
◎瞭解結構抗震、抗風
◎瞭解結構系統與建築規劃設計之整合。

crs_outline:
Foundation Drawing and Model Course for New M.Arch I Students
本課程適合學士後建築新生修習，從基本圖學原理到模型製作技巧，循序漸進地建立設計表現所需的基礎知識與實作能力。課程將於暑假期間密集進行，讓同學能在開學前建立紮實的空間圖學與模型操作能力。開學後則會視同學設計課程的進度與負荷，安排適當時段進行補充教學，以小型工作坊的形式，進一步熟悉各種建築表現技術與工具操作。

圖學部分的重點，在於建立三維空間與二維圖面之間的符號轉換能力與空間敏感度。課程內容涵蓋建築構件與牆體介面的硬體圖學表達、空間中的活動序列與空間感的詮釋方法，以及綜合圖說製作的技巧。每次課程會以雙主軸方式進行：一方面訓練基本圖學邏輯與繪圖精準度，另一方面讓學生運用不同媒材進行個人化的空間詮釋與視覺傳達練習。

模型操作則著重於「安全性、精準性、設計製造、模型表現」四大主題，從建築模型的製作原理到灌模、材料創作等技術引導，鼓勵學生探索不同材料的特性與加工方式，強化工藝能力，同時拓展設計表達的層次與想像力，為後續設計課程打下穩固的技術與美學基礎。

Professional design development encompasses a diverse range of careers, spanning from the idealistic to the pragmatic and from the academic to the industrial. Regardless of the specific profession, the ability to conduct design research and possess knowledge of design science is becoming increasingly vital. In architectural schools, while digital media is widely utilized for design representation and simulations, and despite the vast amount of information available online, there remains a significant gap in our proficiency to make informed design decisions and identify emerging design challenges.

This course is designed to equip students with the skills and knowledge necessary for design research and thesis writing. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and exercises, students will acquire the essential knowledge and skills needed. Part 1 of the course lays the foundational knowledge for all students. Part 2A is tailored for MS and MArch II students, focusing on advanced design research that emphasizes innovation. Part 2B is designed for MArch I students, concentrating on preparing them to craft a design thesis that encapsulates and curates their academic works.

memo: 補修課程
crs_outline:
本課程的目標 : 
1. 使在和聲與曲式學上程度稍弱之音樂所新生，加強其音樂知性方面統合的能力，以適應所上其它的課程。
2. 為已具備基礎樂理程度之非音樂所學生，欲更深入學習專業音樂理論、音樂展演、音樂創作類課程者，提供統合性之初階課程。
3. 為體現一位完整經驗的音樂家而準備 --- 即理論、實務、創作合一。


本課程分為兩個部份：
一是18、19世紀調性基本理論，包含和聲與分析。引導學生著重聲部導進 (voice-leading) 部份，以結構 (structure) 和擴充 (prolongation) 的觀點去分析調性音樂作品，希望學生不再視調性音樂為一連串孤立和絃的接合，而應探究其意義與功能，視整體為一個有機體 (an organic unity)。
二是風格寫作部份，在於突顯和經驗西方藝術音樂 ( art music )及其一些主要的概念，並藉用它們來創作體現。這些概念包括 : 
1.主題的呈現方式 : sentence / period ，和其它…。
2.Idea作為整體質 (totality) 和其論述 (discourse) 之體現。
3.奏鳴曲中不可或缺的結構事件功能角色 (主題的敘述、發展、對照、結尾…)。
4.音型化 (figuration) 、單一和弦的擴充、結構和聲進行的擴充 (structural harmony prolongation)。
5.音形作為符號 (sign)、作為風格 ( style )、作為題旨(topic)。
6.發展變奏的概念與技巧。

This graduate course introduces research methods, as well as the strategies and the “language” of writing about music to performance majors. We start with a brief review of the basics of research tools and crucial issues in and ethics of academic writing. We continue with a series of sample writings hand in hand with these principles. We will see how the authors focus on different aspects of perspectives in their discussion of music and how they develop and sharpen their arguments. 

The aim of this course is to offer graduate music majors necessary tools and directions to engage in an intelligent discussion of their repertory, skills that they may apply to their term projects, thesis writing, and lecture recitals. The readings included in the syllabus will enable us to see the variety of ways that an author may use to approach a music work. We will have invited music scholars(s) coming to discuss the ways that they phrase they theories arguments.

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
This graduate seminar offers a critical assessment of music in relationship to the supernatural, with case studies ranging from the late eighteenth- to the early twentieth century, often known as the “long nineteenth century,” in European culture. We will explore how standard repertoire in this period ties to the developments in science and technology, including staging technology, Gothic literature, and the aesthetics of ethereal sounds and music instruments. We will also examine how the emphasis on reason in the Enlightenment influenced the reading of the supernatural in this period, and how it linked with the perception and depiction of spirits, as well as the changing image of magician in mass media and cultural industry. 
Whereas the attachment of the supernatural to music is common in this period, only a small number of scholars have undergone in-depth discussion of what it meant to appear and to sound supernatural in the given cultural context. Furthermore, it is oftentimes taken for granted in scholarly discolors that the supernatural plot and characters served as a pretext for the composers to exploit innovative music techniques, timbre, and instrumentation. Whether there need to be a match between the two remains a topic that falls under the radar. Our primary agenda is to view music intertwined with the larger cultural context of the time, which will lead to a broader understanding of what is written in the score and open up questions that may help us go beyond the score. 
English will be the primary language for this course. Explanation of more complex ideas and discussion of the course materials can be conducted bilingually or in Mandarine.

crs_outline:

2. 整個課程設計以西洋調性音樂為基底。其中特別著重在分析西元1700年到1900年這200年間的西洋調性音樂。

1) 從宏觀(macro-)與微觀(micro-)的角度出發，學習樂曲曲式的結構(form structure)與調性和聲的擴張與延展(tonal harmony  
     prolongation)。
2) 瞭解表達調性音樂內容的層級觀念（hierarchical concept），學習製作Formal Diagram (Form Structure) 和 Sketch of 
     Reduction Analysis (Harmonic Progression)。

除上述二個學習目標外，本課程特別注重將所學得的分析方法與技巧，實際地應用在音樂作品分析上。

This course is to learn about early keyboard instruments – Harpsichord. This instrument has played an important role in the history of keyboard music from the 15th to the 18th century. The unique plucking mechanism of the harpsichord requires sensitivity and versatility touch and fingering application. The playing technique, varied repertoire, and literature discussion are the focus of this course.

The instructional objective of this course is to develop basic harpsichord performance skills and to cultivate an understanding of touch and performance practices across different historical periods and regions, thereby enhancing students’ awareness and interpretive insight into the music of each corresponding era.

memo: [English Medium Course]
cos_ename: Computer Music Technique: DSP and Composition
crs_outline:
This is not a course based on commercial music or a specific software:
1)	An overview of history of techniques, ideas, and the aesthetics of electronic music from the beginning of the 20th century through now.
2)	Familiarity with basics of psychoacoustics and the basics of digital audio such as editing, multi-tracking, and mixing
3)	A basic understanding of basic DSP techniques, such as additive, subtractive, and distortion synthesis; microsound; and more advanced mixing techniques
4)	Learning to use a DAW (Reaper recommended – see https://whyreaper.com/) to montage and create complete computer music compositions
5)	Complete reading and listening response assignments about electronic music, create smaller electronic music etudes, create two larger works of computer music, engage in classroom “writers’ workshop”type of discussions, complete both a Midterm and Final
6)	Develop a deeper understanding and vocabulary for a critical understanding of electronic and computer music to enhance whatever one’s interests are – be it performance, composition, electronic music, sound design, and/or multi-media art.  Or as John Cage would say, develop “Happy New Ears”!~
7)	Have fun!~

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
This course introduces fundamental concepts applicable to biomedical instrumentation systems. Topics include the static and dynamic characteristics of measurement systems, the engineering design process, commercial development pathways, regulatory classifications, and electrical safety standards for medical devices. 
The course emphasizes practical design principles, enabling students with limited electronics backgrounds to develop instruments that may not be commercially available. Students will learn the principles underlying various sensor mechanisms, analog signal processing (including amplifier and filter design), and digital data acquisition, processing, storage, and display using microcontrollers. 
Applications covered include cardiovascular and respiratory measurements, biosensors, clinical laboratory instrumentation, medical imaging systems, as well as selected therapeutic and prosthetic devices. 
Course Goals:
1.	Emphasize engineering design principles to enable students to develop medical instrumentation systems.
2.	Provide updated coverage of modern sensor technologies and signal processing techniques.
3.	Introduce contemporary microcontroller applications in biomedical instrumentation.
4.	Present revised and updated chapters, descriptions, and references reflecting current advancements.
5.	Strengthen analytical and problem-solving skills through comprehensive worked examples.
6.	Provide supplementary learning materials via a companion webpage.
7.	Offer a solutions manual containing complete solutions to all problems for instructional support.

crs_outline:
本課程旨在引導學生掌握應對現代複雜系統（如：B5G 衛星通訊系統、先進半導體異質整合、無人機產業、太空計畫）的核心技術與管理方法。本課程以國際系統工程協會 (INCOSE) 最新發布之 Systems Engineering Handbook V5 (SEH v5) 為核心教材，課程架構將導入2026 年 INCOSE SEP (Systems Engineering Professional) 學習計畫，以衛星、半導體、無人機、電機產業實務為案例及習作，協助學生加速獲得相關系統工程知識。
目標是接軌國際最新認證標準、建立層級化系統架構思維、實踐以模型為基礎系統工程 (MBSE)。

memo: 上課教室：ED108
crs_outline: 陽明交通大學電子研究所為培育「類比積體電路(Analog IC)」設計人才，特別成立『乙A組 (類比學群)』招收碩博士研究生。乙A組主修類比積體電路，包括射頻積體電路、微波積體電路、感測與制動積體電路、生醫積體電路、電源管理積體電路、電力電子等，以 analog circuit design 為主。 此Seminar課程，經常邀請學者專家以及業界公司技術主管來進行技術演講與實務經驗分享，讓研究生能進一步了解業界實際應用情況與技術發展現況。

crs_outline:
The course teaches fundamental principles on using band diagrams and carrier transport to analyze bipolar diodes, Schottky diodes, photodiodes, BJT, MOS capacitor, MOSFET and Flash memories. Emphasis is put on the MOSFET designs for aggressively scaled VLSI technology. The economical, environmental and social impacts of the semiconductor technology will be illustrated from the past industrial data and the future prediction. The goal for this course is to train circuit, device and process engineers for semiconductor technology research and development.

cos_cname: 半導體元件可靠度及其失效物理
memo: [English Medium Course](1)開學後加退選階段：開放外系及外校選課；開放填寫google加簽表單且依規定加簽。加簽方式會在第一堂課時說明並提供表單，欲加簽同學第一堂課請務必要來。
cos_ename: Reliability and Failure Physics of Semiconductor Devices
crs_outline:
"Reliability is, after all, engineering in its most practical form" said by James R. Schlesinger - Former US Secretary of State for Defense. Reliability is an essential part of a successful semiconductor product because it is related to trust. No reliability is equal to no business. Especially, the new technologies based on the advanced designs and novel materials, e.g., FinFETs, high k dielectrics, wide bandgap, Ferroelectric, or 2D materials, cannot be commercialized without the proven reliability. Therefore, a good R&D engineer should recognize the statistical tools/characterization methods, identify the reliability issues,and evaluate failure physics, further designing for reliability. In this course, the basic semiconductor devices/processes, statistical tools, and characterization methods for reliability evaluation are covered. Furthermore, four most important main reliability challenges (Bias temperature instability & interface traps / Time dependent dielectric breakdown / Mass transport-induced failures / Electrostatic discharge (ESD)) will be addressed in this class. 

前美國國防部部長 James R. Schlesinger曾說：可靠度是工程中最實際的層面。高可靠度是所有半導體產品成功的重要因素，因為可靠度與客戶對產品的信任有關。沒有可靠度等於沒有客戶的信賴而失去商業價值。對先進的半導體技術，例如FinFET、高介電常數絕緣層、寬能隙、鐵電或二維材料等，如果無法通過可靠度驗證，這些技術將無法商品化。因此，優秀的研發工程師應該具備評估可靠度所需統計工具/量測方法來確定可靠度問題，並評估特性衰退的物理特性，並進一步設計高可靠度產品。本課程中將深入淺出的介紹基本半導體元件/製程及可靠度評估所需的統計工具和量測方法。此外，本課程也將會探討四個最重要也最常見的半導體元件可靠度議題（偏壓溫度不穩定性和界面缺陷 Bias temperature instability & interface traps / 依時性閘極崩潰 Time dependent dielectric breakdown / 質量傳輸引起的故障 Mass transport-induced failures / 靜電放電 ESD）。

Intended Learning Outcomes (ILOs):
By the end of this class, you should be able to:
1. Explain the basic operation principles and fabrication processes for the MOS type semiconductor technologies
2. Apply the basic statistics/statistical tools for reliability analysis 
3. Evaluate the failure physics of reliability issues 
4. Present the reliability issues using your own word
5. Design for reliability (DFR)

預期學習成果：
在本課程結束時，修課的學生能夠：
1.解釋MOS半導體技術的基本工作原理和製程
2.應用基本的統計工具進行可靠度分析
3.評估導致不穩定元件特性的失效物理機制
4.闡述對可靠度問題的見解
5.增強可靠度的元件設計（Design for reliability）

P.S. The course structure was originally designed by Prof. Guido Groeseneken (imec/KU Leuven) for the class “Reliability and Yield in Micro- and Nanoelectronic Components,” which I attended during 09–12/2011. I sincerely appreciate Prof. Groeseneken for his exceptional course and for his guidance that shaped my foundation in the reliability field.

crs_outline:
自1960年代以來，經過數十年的發展，電腦晶片及電子元件相關產品的功能日益強大。藉由縮小電晶體本身的體積與增加運算能力，晶片功能得以不斷的提升，這個晶片的進步基本上依循摩爾定律(Moore's Law)的預測。然而在不久的未來，由於微影技術及物理極限，縮小電晶體的發展將會遇到瓶頸。另外一方面，由於單一晶片上電晶體數目的持續增加及晶片複雜化所造成的總導線(global interconnect)增加，決定晶片表現的關鍵已經由單一電晶體轉為總導線電阻電容延遲(global interconnect RC delay)。最後，隨著對晶片功能要求的提升，整合來自異質基板材料的不同元件的需求也越來越大。為了解決上述的挑戰與需求，遂有三維積體電路(3D ICs)概念的出現。 三維積體電路為下一世代電子產業的新趨勢, 亦為我國及世界各國科技大廠正在努力追求的方向。 本課程將包括下列部分: 三維積體電路的歷史、三維積體電路的概念、三維積體電路的關鍵技術、三維積體電路的優缺點、挑戰, 研究現況、產品。希望透過本課程，能讓學生習得三維積體電路的基本知識及科技應用。若將來有興趣此領域，能夠有足夠的基礎與應用能力。

crs_outline:
Semiconductor technology is at the heart of every advanced electronic system—smartphones, 5G infrastructure, AI accelerators, cloud computing, electric vehicles, and beyond. As these applications surge, the demand for innovative semiconductor devices and materials has never been higher.
This course provides a foundational yet forward-looking introduction to Semiconductor Physics and Devices, the core knowledge required for researchers and engineers in the Semiconductor, IC, optoelectronics, and power electronics industries.
半導體技術是所有先進電子系統的核心——從智慧型手機、5G 基礎建設、AI 加速器、雲端運算到電動車，都不可或缺。隨著這些應用快速成長，對創新半導體元件與材料的需求也達到前所未有的高度。
本課程將從基礎到前瞻，帶來「半導體物理與元件」的完整介紹，這是所有從事半導體、積體電路、光電、電力電子等領域的研究者與工程師必備的核心知識。

We will cover:
1. Fundamental semiconductor material properties
2. Carrier transport: drift, diffusion, and recombination
3. Operating principles of key devices: p–n diode, BJT, MOSFET, and JFET
4. Emerging challenges in device scaling (short-channel effects, ultra-thin dielectrics, SS limits)
5. A forward look into beyond-Moore technologies, including new materials, architectures, and device concepts
By combining rigorous physics with real-world examples and the latest industry trends, the course prepares students for careers in semiconductor R&D, IC design, reliability engineering, and advanced manufacturing.

課程內容涵蓋：
1. 半導體材料的基本特性
2. 載子傳輸機制：漂移、擴散與復合
3. 重要元件的操作原理：p–n 接面二極體、BJT、MOSFET、JFET
4. 元件微縮時所面臨的新挑戰：短通道效應、超薄介電層、次臨界擺幅限制等
5. 超越摩爾定律的前瞻技術，包括新材料、新架構與創新元件概念

本課程透過嚴謹的物理推導、實例分析與產業最新趨勢，協助學生建立扎實的半導體基礎，並為未來在半導體研發、IC 設計、可靠度工程及先進製造領域的職涯發展做好準備。

Intended Learning Outcomes (ILOs)（預期學習成果）
By the end of the course, you will be able to:
1. Explain the essential semiconductor material properties and device physics.
2. Analyze the operating principles of p–n diodes, MOSFETs, BJTs, and JFETs using physical models.
3. Evaluate modern scaling challenges—short-channel effects, ultra-thin dielectrics, subthreshold swing limits—and identify the underlying device-physics problems.
4. Propose innovative device structures or design strategies to address limitations in next-generation semiconductor technologies.
-Innovation begins with understanding and solving the right problems.

預期學期成果:
在本課程結束時，修課的學生能夠：
1.解釋半導體材料特性及元件物理
2.利用元件物理分析半導體原件操作原理。
3.評估在微縮下半導體元件的議題，包含短通道效應、超薄介電層及次臨界擺伏限制。
4.提出元件設計來克服半導體元件發展的挑戰。

crs_outline:
This course aims to convey the senior and graudated EE students techniques to design the VLSI chips using state-of-the-art CAD tools. In addition to learning CAD tools for performance-driven and cost-effective IC designs, a top-down design flow and related environment will also be addressed. Upon completion of the course, the student will be able to design the integrated circuits and systems based on standard cell library as well as full-custom layout approaches. As such he/she will be able to work in a team of designers or stand alone.
The course starts from system design specs of an application which demands the need of developing specific hardwares or application specific integrated circuits (ASIC) or application processors. Then followed by the presentation of architectural proposals, an optimal architecture leading to performance-driven and cost-effective realization can be derived based on both sampling rate and system clock rate. With the support of Verilog-HDL, designers can describe their designs either in behavioral level or structural level. Before going down to the lower level design, one has to do initial floorplan to estimate both routing style and module aspect ratio which provide some area constraints for later designs. Then the partitioned blocks can be conducted hierarchically and with the support of synthesis as well as P&R routing tools, physical layout can easily be achieved if cell-based design approach is exploited. Finally through layout verification and post-layout simulation, the design can be verified before fabrication.

cos_cname: 原子尺度量子電子傳導
crs_outline: 學習原子尺度模擬的基本原理 — 密度泛函理論，以VASP軟體為範例去學習模擬計算原理，達成應用於了解元件材料之原子尺度本質特性的目標；並以密度泛函理論的電子結構計算為出發點，結合非平衡格林函數法去近一步數值計算：包含了「原子尺度」與「量子傳輸」兩項效應之電流對電壓(I-V)的關係。

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
課程時間: M567  
Silicon photonics is an innovative field that merges photonics and electronics to manipulate light on a photonic chip. By leveraging silicon's optical properties, this technology enables the integration of optical components like waveguides, modulators, and detectors directly onto silicon chips. This integration facilitates faster data transmission and processing speeds, lower power consumption, and compact device designs.  This course aims to provide students with a fundamental understanding of silicon photonics, covering key topics such as applications, device properties, and fabrication processes. Students will also gain practical experience by realizing the optical functionalities of waveguides through numerical simulations.

crs_outline:
課程概述：本課程旨在講授半導體元件基本原理，學習半導體元件工作原理與特性。課程並簡介這些元件之技術與應用。此為電機資訊學院跨領域研究之基礎。
課程目標：
一、了解半導體元件之物理與基本觀念。
二、學習二極體、金屬半導體接面、金屬絕緣體半導體電容、雙極性接面電晶體、金屬氧化物半導體場效應電晶體之基本原理與特性。
三、了解積體電路元件相關應用。

crs_outline: The fundamentals of discrete-time (digital) signal processing will be introduced in this course. Students will learn how to represent discrete-time signals and systems and analyze them using mathematical tools including discrete-time Fourier transform, z-transform, and discrete Fourier transform. Practical aspects such as structures or implementations for discrete-time systems, filter design methods, and fast Fourier transform will be also covered.

In this course, we will introduce various deep learning architectures and techniques, and discuss the advances in this area through paper presentation (by students). Students have the chance to practice implementing deep learning by doing programming homework and applying deep learning to real problems by doing final project.

dep_ename: Department of Electronics and Electrical Engineering
crs_outline: This course provides the basic design and analysis of wireless communications systems. The topics range from wireless propagation channel, digital communication design and analysis, multiple access schemes, cell planning, MIMO, NOMA, etc. Students taking this course should especially learn (i) basic properties of wireless channels, such as fading and delay dispersion; (ii) basic digital communication for wireless systems, such as BER analysis in fading channels; (iii) methods that help dealing with wireless challenges, such as diversity; (iv) multi-user and multi-cell wireless systems; (v) advanced wireless techniques, such as MIMO and D2D communications; (vi) the ability to studying and investigating cutting-edge wireless communication systems, such as 5G and 6G systems.

dep_ename: Department of Electronics and Electrical Engineering
crs_outline:
新興的下世代 5G/6G 關鍵前導技術 (包含 IoT, M2M, HetNet D2D offloading) 本質上皆是以無線隨意網路的形式運作，本課程內容涵蓋無線隨意網路相關熱門研究主題，介紹及引導各主題可能之研究方向，並包含手動實驗及模擬工具學習，讓同學兼具無線網路知識與研究思考驗證能力。

Emerging next-generation 5G/6G technologies, including IoT, M2M communications, and heterogeneous network (HetNet) D2D offloading, are essentially required to operate in the form of wireless ad hoc networks. This course has been designed for graduate or pre-graduate students pursuing advanced research study with a special interest in wireless ad hoc networks. Students are encouraged to have a basic understanding of the layered TCP/IP architecture before signing up. Our purpose is to bring a variety of hot research topics to the table, so that students working on (or still uncertain about) this area can acquire the necessary research knowledge and skills through the provided course materials.

memo: [English Medium Course]
dep_ename: Department of Electronics and Electrical Engineering
crs_outline:
This course is quantum statistical mechanics. 
Quantum Mechanics (535366) and Statistical Mechanics (535368) are combined classes to teach quantum physics. 

As well-known, quantum physics is the basic scholar of modern science and technologies. It may be difficult for anyone to be a premier in nanotechnologies without the precise knowledge of quantum physics. However, what is  "quantum" appears quite strange to beginners. This class is then an introductory quantum physics for engineering students. In particular, we will hit what/how many guys misunderstand about quantum physics. For example, to solve Schrodinger equation differs from to know quantum physics. This just corresponds to the essence of quantum physics.  In quantum mechanics (535366), we will discuss mainly one quantum particle systems (ex., an electron). In Statistical Mechanics (535368), we will discuss many quantum particles system.  

NOTE: strongly recommend to attend the Statistical Mechanics (535366), too. 

I illustrate: 
1) relationship between quantum mechanics and device engineering, 
2) what the wavefunction is. 
3) what to solve Schrodinger equation is.--- what the observation is. 
4) several methods to solve Schrodinger equation.

crs_outline:
本課程以大型語言模型（LLM）與生成式 AI 應用系統為核心，系統性介紹 Transformer、Prompt 設計與 structured outputs、工具/函式呼叫、context engineering（RAG、hybrid search、reranking、long context 與 context caching）、PEFT/LoRA、多模態理解與生成、agent workflows、evaluation、部署、安全/隱私/法遵，以及智慧醫療與跨域案例。課程強調「系統工程」與「可驗證評估」，期末以專題方式完成一個可展示、可評估、可說明風險的生成式 AI 系統。
本課程主要目標：
1. 理解生成式 AI 的核心概念與發展脈絡（Transformer/LLM、多模態、agents）。
2. 具備建構 LLM 應用系統的能力（prompt、structured outputs、tool use、context engineering、微調、部署）。
3. 掌握模型可靠性與品質評估（事實性、引用、幻覺、成本、延遲）及安全/隱私/法遵議題。
4. 以專題形式完成需求定義、資料治理、系統實作、測試、報告與展示之全流程。
This course covers generative AI from both model and system perspectives, including LLMs, multimodal models, tool use, context engineering, agents, evaluation, deployment, and governance.

crs_outline: 矽光子學使用矽為主的光學材料製作積體光路(Photonic integrated circuit)，特別是可採用現今已高度成熟的半導體製程，具有可量產化的優勢。目前已運用於資料傳輸上，以光取代電的方式，提供更高的頻寬予通訊、數據中心及電腦運算科技。未來可望在晶片中整合積體光路和積體電路，在晶片中實現完整的光電系統。此外，矽光子元件具有微型化、可重構（reconfigurable）的特性，目前產生許多新興應用，如光學雷達和生醫感測器等等。本課程將介紹波導相關的光學原理、各種被動及主動元件、製程技術，培養學生進入矽光子學研究所需的知識。

The class starts from the classical description of optical transmission and reflection followed by the quantum mechanical description of optical absorption and emission in materials and effect of excitons. The materials mentioned throughout this class include semiconductors, metals, low dimensional material and organic materials. Therefore, the objective of this class is to teach student to understand the classical treatment of optical propagation in the solid materials, quantum mechanical treatment of absorption and emission in materials, the importance of the exciton in the materials, and the origin of the optical nonlinear effect in the crystals.

cos_ename: High-Performance and Quantum Computing: Applications and Implementation
crs_outline:
本課程以「高速計算與量子計算之應用與實作」為主題，旨在引導學生理解後摩爾時代的計算趨勢，並掌握高效能計算（HPC）與量子計算（QC）的核心概念與實作方法。課程內容涵蓋平行計算、GPU加速運算、量子計算基礎與量子電路模擬、量子優化演算法，以及量子機器學習等主題。學生將透過理論講授與程式實作，建立從傳統高速計算到量子計算的整合性知識架構，並以Qiskit、CUDA-Q等工具在遠端高速運算叢集（HPC cluster）上進行實作與專題演練。
課程目標：
1. 建立高速計算與量子計算的理論基礎概念；2. 能在遠端高速運算叢集上進行平行與加速運算實作與效能評估；3. 能開發程式完成量子電路建構與模擬；4. 能整合跨領域方法，完成量子優化與量子機器學習的應用案例；5. 透過專題實作與成果展示，培養問題解決與團隊合作能力。

crs_outline:
本課程以 NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute（DLI）之專業課程為核心，系統性介紹現代深度學習與生成式AI之理論與實務應用。課程涵蓋深度學習基礎、自然語言處理（NLP）、生成式AI（Generative AI）、大型語言模型（LLM）以及Agentic AI等關鍵技術，並強調實作導向之學習模式。

學生將透過五大主題模組逐步建立完整能力，包括：
1.深度學習基本概念與神經網路訓練方法
2.自然語言處理與語意理解技術
3.生成式AI模型（如Diffusion Model等）
4.AI Agent與應用系統整合（Agentic AI / RAG）
5.大型語言模型之預訓練與微調
本課程強調「從理論到實作」，學生將透過實驗環境與實作專案，培養以下能力：
理解深度學習與生成式AI核心原理
能夠使用現代AI框架進行模型開發與應用
建立AI系統設計能力（包含LLM與Agent整合）
掌握產業最新趨勢（如AI Agent、Physical AI）

本課程將有助於學生銜接學術研究與產業應用，並具備進入AI相關領域之基礎能力。

cos_ename: Formal Languages and Theory of Computation
crs_outline:
The Ultimate Question: What inherently makes some problems computationally effortless while others remain frustratingly difficult?

Despite five decades of intense research, computer scientists still don't have a definitive answer to this question. However, this pursuit has yielded a massive breakthrough: an elegant classification framework that categorizes problems based on their intrinsic difficulty.

This theoretical blueprint has directly revolutionized the ancient field of cryptography. By intentionally building security systems around these certified "hard" problems, cryptographers have successfully engineered entirely new, ultra-secure codes.

crs_outline:
Software testing is to exercise the program using input data in three different space domains: (1) in the requirement and specification domain, (2) in the program implementation domain, (3) in the test input space domain.  The space covered in (1), (2), (3) will intersect one another and exhibit different properties to reveal the software defects, quality of use, and potential exploitation. Our course will cover several conventional software testing issues: 1. Functional testing, 2. Structural testing, 3. Integration and system testing. Other than these, test plans used in Microsoft and google will be discussed. Nonconventional testing like fuzzing , exploitable testing and symbolic execution will be introduced too.
軟體測試是以輸入資料來操作程式，針對三種不同的範圍來討論: (1) 規格需求的範圍,(2) 程式實作的範圍, (3) 輸入資料的空間範圍。這三種空間的範圍，彼此交集，也呈現不同的特性，展現程式本身的缺陷、品質與可能隱含的資安操作空間。我們的課程將涵蓋傳統測試議題:1. 功能性測試, 2. 結構化測試, 3. 整合與系統測試。同時，我們也介紹微軟與 Google 相關軟體的測試過程，並涵蓋非典型的如 fuzzing、脅迫測試與符號執行測試。

cos_cname: 敏捷軟體工程：產品探索、開發流程與測試實務
memo: 資訊學院優先。
cos_ename: Agile Software Engineering: Product Discovery, Development Process, and Testing Practices
crs_outline:
在真實軟體開發團隊中，「寫程式」只是整體流程的一小部分。更關鍵的，是如何探索產品需求、協作開發、持續交付並確保品質。
本課程以 「敏捷軟體工程」 為核心，結合 Scrum、Kanban、Agile Product Discovery、Agile Testing、Specification by Example、Exploratory Testing 與 LeSS（Large-Scale Scrum）等方法，讓學生從真實案例與實作中理解現代軟體團隊的運作方式。
課程強調「從產品想法到交付的完整生命週期」，學生將學習如何在跨職能團隊中協作，如何將需求轉化為可驗證的規格（Spec），以及如何透過測試策略提升軟體的可靠性與可持續性。
這門課不僅教你如何「開發軟體」，更教你如何「用工程思維創造價值」。
完成本課程後，學生將能夠：
1.	理解敏捷軟體工程的核心原則與價值觀
認識 Scrum、Kanban、LeSS 等框架背後的工程哲學與組織行為。
2.	運用 Agile Product Discovery 技術探索需求
透過假設驗證、用戶訪談與 Pretotyping，縮短從想法到實證的距離。
3.	設計與管理開發流程
建立具可視化的工作流程與研發節奏，理解研發效能（Engineering Productivity）的衡量方式。
4.	應用測試導向的工程實務
掌握 Agile Testing、Specification by Example、Exploratory Testing 等方法，設計高價值的測試活動。
5.	協作與擴展敏捷團隊
了解如何在多團隊環境中運用 LeSS 原則協作，並在不同角色間（PM、RD、QA）建立共識與對齊。

dep_ename: Graduate Program of College of Computer Science
crs_outline:
邊緣人工智慧：邊緣人~工作的智慧？邊緣人工~的智慧？邊緣的~人工智慧！

不管怎麼解讀，概念都離不開 efficient (高效率) 這個詞，尤其對 CS 領域的邊緣人來說，能躺著幹就不坐起來，能坐著幹就不站起來，實為 efficient 一詞的極致表現。身為 CS 領域的(邊緣)人，如果你對人工智慧有興趣，但不想再調參建模了，此課必修！

========
當人工智慧越來越普及，越來越多的人工智慧服務將被去中心化，也就是邊緣化，邊緣化的人工智慧服務仰賴邊緣(終端)裝置獨立運作，可不仰賴網路連接至大型雲端伺服器或資料中心，更不須分享機敏資料。相較於集中式的、雲端的人工智慧服務，邊緣化的人工智慧服務(此後簡稱為邊緣人工智慧)有以下幾項優點：
1. 高隱私性、無機敏資料洩漏之疑慮
2. 無(低)網路需求、不受網路頻寬影響
3. 無(低)雲端伺服器或資料中心之需求

但天下沒有白吃的午餐，想當邊緣人，凡事就得自己來；想擁有邊緣人工智慧的優點，凡事只能靠在地的、非雲端的邊緣(終端)裝置。然而，終端裝置通常不具備大規模運算能力，沒有充沛的記憶體資源，且可能沒有穩定的電力來源甚至僅依賴電池供電。因此，邊緣人工智慧的運行，必須高效率，更精確地說，軟體(人工智慧之模型)要小巧但準確，硬體(運行人工智慧之裝置)要又快又省電，缺一不可。

這門課將探討一系列為了實現「邊緣人工智慧」的相關技術，詳細內容請看下面的進度列表。

crs_outline: 這門課首先將介紹為了在無線行動網路中提供多媒體應用與物聯網應用, TCP/IP各層協定衍生的挑戰以及所需的網路協定。此外，由於多媒體應用對頻寬資源需求明顯提升, 以及萬物聯網所產生的巨量連線，我們第二部分將介紹多項WiFi與5G/B5G新興網路技術與標準。最後, 此課程將介紹軟體定義網路與雲端系統的概念, 以及整合課程介紹的網路協定, 前瞻通訊技術, 軟體定義網路與雲端系統, 讓學生們對5G Core network/Cloud RAN/Open RAN等架構有一整體概念.

cos_cname: 開源核心網路設計與實作
memo: 資訊學院優先。
cos_ename: Open-Source Core Network Design and Implementation
crs_outline:
本課程以培養 5G 行動通訊人才為目標。核心網路在 5G 通訊網路中扮演著不可或缺的角色，開發網路元件需要具備豐富的領域知識（SDN / Network Programming / OS...）。本課程除了涵蓋前面提到的知識以外，更會以淺入深出帶領學生體驗核心網路的開發與知識。

本課程將以 free5GC 開源軟體為主體，此軟體為陳志成教授領導開發的核心網路開源軟體，是全世界第一個開源的 5G 核心網路專案，並於 2024 年 9 月 16 日加入全球開源軟體領導組織 — Linux 基金會，為 5G 網路的研究與發展帶來強大的平台與資源。

This course aims to cultivate professionals in the field of 5G mobile communications. The core network plays an essential role in 5G communication networks, and developing core network functions requires extensive domain knowledge in areas such as Software-Defined Networking (SDN), network programming, and operating systems (OS). In addition to covering these fundamental topics, the course will guide students step by step, from basic concepts to hands-on experience in 5G core network development.

The course will primarily use free5GC, an open-source 5G core network project led by Professor Jyh-Cheng Chen. free5GC is the world’s first open-source 5G core network project and joined the Linux Foundation on September 16, 2024. By becoming part of the Linux Foundation ecosystem, free5GC provides a powerful platform and greater resources for the research, development, and advancement of 5G networks.

cos_cname: 軟體定義網路及網路功能虛擬化
memo: 資訊學院優先。
cos_ename: Software Defined Networks and Network Function Virtualization
crs_outline:
本課程探討軟體定義網路(Software-Defined Networking, SDN)與網路功能虛擬化(Network Function Virtualization, NFV)的核心原理與實作。內容涵蓋:高速網路的效能量測方法學、OpenFlow/match-action 統一抽象、Linux 核心資料路徑與調校(NAPI、RSS/RPS、offload、TCP/AQM)、核心旁路與可程式資料面(DPDK、eBPF/XDP、Open vSwitch、P4)，並延伸至 NFV 的 MANO 架構與電信/資料中心 NFV(CORD、service chaining)，說明如何把軟體資料面做到快到足以取代硬體。學生透過四個實驗與一個期末論文重現專題，建立「從封包旅程到線速轉發」的完整實作能力。
目標:
(1) 理解 control/data plane 分離與 SDN 的統一抽象
(2) 能量測與調校高速網路資料路徑
(3) 能用 OpenFlow/OVS/P4/XDP 實作並比較可程式資料面
(4) 理解 NFV 與 MANO,能實作 SDN 加速的網路功能(learning switch、virtual router)
(5) 能重現並改進一篇系統網路論文。

Students will study the complete video-coding pipeline, from color representation, transform coding, quantization, entropy coding, and motion compensation to rate-distortion optimization and the design of modern video-coding standards. Students will implement key coding tools, analyze compression-performance trade-offs, and use real-world tools to evaluate modern codecs and streaming systems.

dep_ename: Graduate Program of College of Computer Science
crs_outline:
課程內容兼具理論、技術、實務、與系統實習。課程內容涵蓋設計、製作一個3D遊戲所需的程式設計。除了理論與技術之學習之外，學生需完成一個term project，在一個3D遊戲引擎核心之上加上自己的程式模組，以設計一個3D遊戲。

The course content combines theory, technology, practice, and system implementation. The course content covers the programming required to design and produce a 3D game. In addition to learning theory and technology, students need to complete a term project and add their own program modules to a 3D game engine to design a 3D game.

Intended learning outcomes (ILOs)
After learning from this course, the students are expected to be able to
+ Describe the process of game development
+ Explain game system architectures
+ Describe the basic techniques in games
+ Integrate basic techniques into comprehensive systems
+ Identify the problems in game development
+ Apply techniques to solve problems
+ Analyze architectures of systems
+ Evaluate game performance
+ Create a game using various techniques

The students are expected to enhance/improve the following skills: 1) programming, 2) source code reading and comprehension, 3) report writing, 4) teamwork, and oral presentation.

Game Engine: We will use a stable version Unity to learn basic programming skills for games.
Platform: Visual Studio or other editors. Students should be familiar with Unity, C# Programming.  

The students will learn how to implement some game concepts in Unity.

crs_outline: This course explores pattern recognition through the lens of geometric spaces and representation learning. Moving beyond static algorithms, students study how computers structure raw high-dimensional data into meaningful geometry—covering metric engineering, non-linear manifold unrolling, probabilistic latent density fields, and the mathematical mechanics used to audit modern self-supervised foundation embeddings. This is a revised design that shifts away from traditional approaches focused on classification methods or neural networks, with the goal that the students will gain a more unified understanding, instead of just a toolbox of algorithms and/or models.

dep_cname: 量子科學與工程碩士學位學程
dep_ename: Master Program in Quantum Science and Technology
crs_outline:
本課程為量子碩士學位學程之必修課程，目標是為來自電機、光電、物理、資訊等不同背景之新生建立量子科技的整體圖像。課程分為三大單元：（一）量子計算及量子電路；（二）量子光學與量子感測；（三）量子晶片元件。
修畢本課程後，學生應能掌握量子位元、量子閘與量子演算法之基本概念；說明關鍵量子光學實驗（HOM 干涉、Bell 測試）與量子感測原理（量子 Fisher 資訊、標準量子極限）；並瞭解量子晶片元件之工作原理與量子科技之國際發展現況。

dep_ename: Master Program in Quantum Science and Technology
crs_outline: 為培育量子相關人才，包括推動量子科學與工程跨領域發展，涵蓋量子計算、量子通訊等核心技術，本課程邀請學者專家以及業界公司技術主管來進行技術演講與實務經驗分享外並安排本學程學生進行實驗研究報告。

cos_ename: Contemporary Research of Neurotechnology and Neural Engineering
dep_cname: 腦科技跨領域工程碩士學位學程
dep_ename: Interdisciplinary Master's Program in Brain Technology
crs_outline:
本課程整合神經工程(Neural Engineering)與腦科技(Neurotechnology)之核心概念與前沿發展，探討如何透過工程方法與系統設計，實現對神經系統之量測(read)、解碼(decode)、調控(modulate)與重建(repair)。
課程將涵蓋從基礎神經訊號量測、腦機介面(BCI)、神經調控技術，到神經植入式裝置與生醫材料介面，並延伸至工智慧輔助神經解碼、閉迴路神經系統(closed-loop systems)等新興議題。
目標：
1.	建立神經工程與腦科技整合理解
2.	熟悉神經訊號量測與神經調控之關鍵技術
3.	理解腦機介面與神經植入裝置之設計原理
4.	掌握 AI 與機器學習在神經訊號解析之應用
5.	探討未來腦科技發展趨勢

THINKING Logic: Because of the way computers and code operate (strict causality), there is no way to remove logic from most of a programmer's day's work.

dep_cname: 國際半導體產業學院博士班
crs_outline:
The course covers materials science and solid-state physics for macro- to nanoscale electronic devices, with a primary focus on their resistive and conductive properties. Particular attention is devoted to the fundamental physical mechanisms underlying various memory technologies, analyzed from the perspective of barrier profiles and switching phenomena in FeRAM, ReRAM, and MRAM devices.
The operating principles of spin-based magnetic electronic devices are also discussed, including magnetic domain walls in nanowires, skyrmion-related resistance effects, magnetic vortices, spin-transfer torque phenomena, and related concepts.
Seminars and homework assignments include elements of device modeling and numerical simulation using high-level computational tools such as Wolfram Mathematica and MATLAB.

crs_outline:
Course Description

This course introduces the fundamental semiconductor physics underlying modern energy-conversion technologies. Students will learn how quantum mechanics, electronic band structures, density of states (DOS), carrier statistics, and charge transport govern the behavior of semiconductor materials. The course emphasizes the analysis of metal–semiconductor contacts, p–n junctions, heterojunctions, and semiconductor–electrolyte interfaces, and their roles in determining charge separation and transfer in solar cells, photoelectrochemical water-splitting systems, and related energy applications.

Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Explain the fundamental concepts of quantum mechanics, electronic band structures, and density of states in semiconductor materials.

• Analyze carrier distributions, Fermi levels, and charge transport processes in intrinsic and doped semiconductors.

• Interpret and construct energy-band diagrams for metals, semiconductors, metal–semiconductor contacts, p–n junctions, and heterojunctions.

• Evaluate charge separation, carrier transport, and recombination mechanisms using band alignment and density-of-states analysis.

• Analyze the effects of junction design and interfacial electronic structure on device performance.

• Apply thermodynamic and kinetic principles to charge-transfer processes in semiconductor-based energy systems.

• Assess semiconductor materials and interfaces for applications in photovoltaic devices, photoelectrochemical water splitting, photocatalysis, and related renewable-energy technologies.

crs_outline: Compact models serve as a bridge or a translator between the physics-based half of the semiconductor industry (devices and foundries) and its computer-based half (EDA tools and IC design). This course will comprehensively cover the physics and modeling aspects of semiconductor devices, including MOS capacitors and MOSFETs, along with their non-ideal effects. The course aims to delve into the strategies for developing models that meet the industry's requirements for accuracy, computational speed, and robustness. Students will be introduced to industry-standard models such as BSIM-BULK and BSIM-CMG and will also learn benchmarking tests for compact models. Additionally, the course will familiarize students with EDA tools, including SPICE, Verilog-A hardware description language, and ICCAP parameter extraction software, preparing them for real-world applications.

本課程聚焦動態系統的建模、模擬、估測與最佳化，涵蓋以下核心內容：
1. 建模方法：基於物理機理與數據融合驅動的動態系統建模方法，包含時域/頻域參數化建模、機器學習與深度神經網路建模，以及其對應的數學函式解析與理論推導。

The focus of this course is on modeling, simulation, estimation, and optimization of dynamic systems. Concepts taught in this course include physics-based and empirical modeling, dynamic modeling, machine learning and model-free reinforcement learning. For this purpose, the methods to mathematically describe time-evolving systems, the method of system modeling and design of controller for mechanical and electrical engineering systems, machine learning classification and regression are applied.

課程目標:

memo: 建議修過普通物理，微積分及工程數學。
crs_outline:
自旋電子學（Spintronics）利用電子自旋進行感測、資訊儲存與運算，已廣泛應用於磁場感測器、磁性記憶體、神經型態運算及量子感測等領域。本課程將介紹自旋電子學之基本物理原理、磁性薄膜材料、磁阻效應、自旋軌道耦合與磁化動力學等核心概念，並探討其於智慧感測與新型運算架構中的應用。
除理論基礎外，本課程強調實驗實作與研究訓練。學生將接觸磁性薄膜製備、磁性量測與自旋動力學分析技術，包括實際操作超高真空磁控濺鍍系統（Ultra-High Vacuum Magnetron Sputtering）、磁光克爾效應量測（Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect, MOKE）及自旋轉矩鐵磁共振量測（Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance, ST-FMR）等實驗平台，學習自旋電子元件從材料製備、元件特性分析到感測應用之完整研究流程。
課程亦將介紹磁阻式感測器、磁性記憶體、磁振子元件及新興量子磁感測技術，使學生掌握自旋電子感測與智慧計算之最新研究發展與未來趨勢。

課程目標 :
1. 理解自旋電子學之基本物理原理與磁性材料特性。
2. 熟悉GMR、TMR、STT、SOT等重要自旋電子效應及元件操作機制。
3. 瞭解磁性感測器、MRAM及新型智慧計算元件之設計原理與應用。
4. 學習磁性薄膜之製程技術與材料特性分析方法。
5. 實際操作超高真空磁控濺鍍系統（UHV Magnetron Sputtering），了解磁性薄膜與異質結構之製備流程。
6. 實際進行磁光克爾效應（MOKE）量測，分析磁滯曲線、磁異向性與磁化反轉行為。
7. 認識並操作自旋轉矩鐵磁共振（ST-FMR）量測系統，學習磁化動力學與自旋軌道力矩分析方法。
8. 培養進入自旋電子、磁性感測、量子感測及智慧計算相關研究領域之基礎能力。
Spintronics exploits the spin degree of freedom of electrons for sensing, information storage, and computation, and has been widely applied in magnetic sensors, magnetic memory devices, neuromorphic computing, and quantum sensing technologies. This course introduces the fundamental physical principles of spintronics, including magnetic thin-film materials, magnetoresistive effects, spin–orbit coupling, and magnetization dynamics. The course further explores the applications of spintronic devices in intelligent sensing systems and emerging computing architectures.

In addition to theoretical foundations, the course emphasizes hands-on laboratory training and research-oriented learning. Students will gain experience in magnetic thin-film fabrication, magnetic characterization, and spin dynamics analysis through direct operation of advanced experimental platforms, including an Ultra-High Vacuum (UHV) Magnetron Sputtering System, Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) Measurement System, and Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (ST-FMR) Measurement System. Through these activities, students will learn the complete research workflow of spintronic devices, from material synthesis and device characterization to sensing applications.

The course also covers magnetoresistive sensors, magnetic memory technologies, magnonic devices, and emerging quantum sensing techniques, enabling students to understand the latest developments and future trends in spintronic sensing and intelligent computing.

Course Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

Understand the fundamental physical principles of spintronics and the properties of magnetic materials.
Explain the operating mechanisms of key spintronic effects and devices, including GMR, TMR, STT, and SOT.
Understand the design principles and applications of magnetic sensors, MRAM, and emerging intelligent computing devices.
Learn fabrication techniques and characterization methods for magnetic thin films.
Operate an Ultra-High Vacuum (UHV) Magnetron Sputtering System and understand the fabrication processes of magnetic thin films and heterostructures.
Perform Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect (MOKE) measurements and analyze magnetic hysteresis loops, magnetic anisotropy, and magnetization reversal behavior.
Understand and perform Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (ST-FMR) measurements for the investigation of magnetization dynamics and spin–orbit torques.
Develop the fundamental skills required for research in spintronics, magnetic sensing, quantum sensing, and intelligent computing.

「太空動力學」英文為Astrodynamics，其主要研究範疇為在牛頓運動定律與重力定律下，火箭、飛彈與太空飛行器的運動行為。太空動力學主要關心各種太空飛行器從發射、入軌到重返大氣層的運動軌跡，同時也包括了軌道轉換與星際飛行。「太空動力學」是以天體力學為基礎，隨著人類發射第一顆人造衛星Sputnik-1後逐步發展，加入許多新的元素，包括火箭推進、空氣動力學、衛星工程等不同學門，成為一門綜合性的學科。

微流體系統提供了一個方便的自動化平台供多種生物醫療相關的研究與微奈米機器人開發。許多商業產品相應而生主要因為微流體系統的低感染、低成本、高速等種種優點。本課程將從最基礎微流體系統開始介紹。並從知名期刊以及研討會中挑選論文，在課堂中以互動的方式討論。透過此課程學生不只能夠對微流體系統與趨勢有初步的認識，並能了解怎麼去搜尋、閱讀、並審查一般科學文獻。[本門課為英文授課]

Microfluidic system provides a convenient platform of automation for biological and medical tests as well as the development of micor-nano scale robots. Different products have been developed in the market because of its advantages of low-contamination, low-cost, high-speed and etc. In this course, we will first introduce the fundamentals of microfluidic systems. After that, we will interactively discuss the cutting-edge technologies from selected works from journals or top-rank conferences. Through this course, students will 
- Identify and describe the fundamental concepts of microfluidics.
- Apply microfluidic principles to analyze biological and medical systems.
- Critique and evaluate recent microfluidics papers.
- Design and present a novel microfluidic system for a biomedical application.

crs_outline: Animals can move and adapt effectively to complex environment and missions. While soft muscles power the animal movements, they are also leveraged by rigid and elastic mechanisms. This inspired the recent development of bioinspired robots powered by soft actuators through elastic mechanisms. The objective of this course is to teach students the foundation of animal movements, muscles and elastic mechanism, and bioinspired soft actuators. Also taught are the rubber hyperelasticty and transduction principles that enable the smart design of soft robots. In addition, students will have chance to learn the hands-on experiments of making and driving dielectric elastomer-based grippers and locomotor, in addition to the design of flapping wing micro air vehicles.

memo: 核心選修課程  開4/研
crs_outline:
本課程學習以時域/頻域之數學函數分析與理論推導方式進行訊號與系統之處理與轉換,以協助解決實際工程設計問題, 課程內容為
1. 時域/頻域訊號表示方式與系統構成之基本觀念，訊號之捲積（convolution）演算。
2. Fourier, Laplace, Z 轉換之數理函數理論發展, 包括
  -Fourier series and transform: CTFS/DTFS/CTFT/DTFT/DFT/FFT/Short time FT(音訊分析).
  -Laplace transform 及 系統建模
  -取樣定理，訊號混疊 (Aliasing) 
  -Z 轉換及離散時間系統建模
3. 數位濾波器架構, IIR/FIR 濾波器設計與程式實現
4. 瞭解工程或物理現象與數學描述模式之間的關係
5. 如何將訊號與系統理論設計逐步實現在實際工程應用: FFT 程式,數位濾波器程式,PID控制器程式
This course contains a comprehensive treatment of continuous-time and discrete-time signals,systems and transforms, from their theoretical mathematical foundations to practical implementation in engineering.
1. Signals and systems mathematical definition, the characteristics and the properties. Convolution of signals.
2. Fourier Series (FS), Fourier Transform (FT), and analysis in continuous and discrete time domain, including
  -CTFS/DTFS/CTFT/DTFT/DFT/FFT/Short Time FT.
  -Laplace Transform and System Modeling.
  -z-transform and Discrete-Time System Modeling.
3. Digital filter structures and Digital filters design: IIR/FIR
4. Applications to digital signal processing and control
5. FFT programming, Digital Filters programming, PID controller programming

cos_cname: 深度學習與地下水模擬
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
地下水為重要的水資源，約莫供應人類三分之一的用水需求。然而，過度抽取地下水導致地層下陷、海水入侵及土壤鹽化等環境災害。為良好管理地下水資源及防災，準確的地下水模擬十分重要。第三次人工智慧浪潮下，深度學習進一步地融合大數據型態的多樣性(Data variety)，如影像、聲音及文字，可以帶給地下水模擬更多的可能性。本課程目標為介紹人工智慧在地下水模擬上的相關應用，使學生具備應用深度學習於地下水管理及防災之能力。 
Groundwater is a crucial water resource, supplying approximately one-third of human water needs. However, excessive extraction of groundwater has led to environmental disasters such as land subsidence, seawater intrusion, and soil salinization. To effectively manage groundwater resources and prevent disasters, accurate groundwater modeling is essential. In the third wave of artificial intelligence, Deep Learning integrates the variety of big data types, such as image, sound, and text, offering more possibilities for groundwater modeling. The objective of this course is to introduce the applications of artificial intelligence in groundwater modeling, enabling students to apply deep learning in groundwater management and disaster prevention.

crs_outline: Physical and chemical characterization principles are broadly used in materials science and engineering. Surface and interface characterization is a major subject in nanotechnology, heterogeneous catalysis, semiconductor devices, functional materials, corrosion, energy missions, and tribology, etc. This course will study the physical and chemical principles of representative characterization methods frequently used in these research areas. The topics include surface chemistry and physics fundamentals, electron-based and x-ray spectroscopy, vibrational spectroscopy, ellipsometry, microscopy with atomic-scale probes, and data analysis. Students will learn a foundation in the use of characterization techniques to solve and diagnose material problems related to composition, structure, defects, and surfaces that can be identified and potentially resolved with materials characterization.

crs_outline: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the principles and applications of magnetic materials. It begins with the fundamental concepts of magnetism, including magnetic moments, magnetic fields, and magnetic susceptibility. The classification of magnetic behaviors such as diamagnetism, paramagnetism, ferromagnetism, antiferromagnetism, and ferrimagnetism will be explored in detail, emphasizing their physical origins and distinguishing characteristics. A focused examination of ferromagnetism will cover critical concepts such as exchange interaction, magnetic anisotropy, domain formation, and domain wall dynamics, providing a deeper understanding of magnetic ordering and its implications in material behavior. The course also includes case studies on advanced magnetic systems, including magnetic nanostructures, magnetic semiconductors, and spintronics. The emerging field of spintronic devices, with a special focus on magnetoresistive random-access memory (MRAM) technology, will be discussed to highlight real-world applications of magnetic materials in data storage and logic devices. By the end of the course, students will gain both theoretical insights and practical knowledge essential for understanding and working with magnetic materials in research and technological applications.

cos_ename: Advanced Semiconductor Technologies and Global Industry Strategies
dep_ename: Department of Materials Science and Engineering
crs_outline: The course aims to provide students with comprehensive knowledge and practical skills across various aspects of semiconductor technology. Students will explore characterization techniques and their applications in analyzing material properties, learn statistical tools to evaluate device reliability, and address critical challenges such as dielectric breakdown and bias instability. The course also covers radiation effects on semiconductors, 2D materials' unique properties and applications, and the design and operation of optoelectronic devices. Additionally, students will delve into advanced topics such as spintronics, ferroic materials, and their device applications. The curriculum emphasizes the semiconductor industry's evolution, including R&D management, global supply chain dynamics, and business models. Finally, the course fosters creative problem-solving skills, equipping students to address complex challenges in the high-tech industry and innovate within a rapidly evolving technological landscape.

crs_outline:

Introduction to organic semiconductors (including dielectric materials), organic optoelectronics (including optical and nonlinear optical materials), AI silicon photonics (including optical fiber and optical modulator materials), and flexible electronics (including polymer packaging composite materials) and the principles and analysis of their components.

課程綱要(Outline)：
A. 材料性質介紹 (Introduction to Properties of Materials)
1. 材料電學性質 (Electrical Properties of Materials)
2. 材料熱學性質 (Thermal Properties of Materials)
3. 材料光學性質 (Optical Properties of Materials)

B. 高分子材料簡介 (Introduction to Polymer Materials)
1. 高分子材料化學 (Polymer Materials Chemistry)
2. 高分子材料物理 (Polymer Materials Physics)
3. 高分子材料應用 (Applications of Polymer Materials)：液晶高分子材料 LC Polymer Materials、導電高分子材料Conducting Polymer Materials、發光二極體高分子材料 Light Emitting Diode (LED) Polymer Materials、非線性光學高分子材料 Nonlinear Optical (NLO) Polymer Materials、電光高分子材料 Electro-Optic (EO) Polymer Materials Materials

1.1.2.	化學結構及物理性質(Chemical Structures and Physical Properties)
2. 液晶之應用物性與量測 (Introduction to LCs)
2.1. 液晶電學及光學性質 (Electrical and Optical Properties of LCs)
2.2. 液晶光電效應 (Electro-Optical Properties of LCs)
3. 液晶顯示相關原理及元件 (Principle and Devices of LCDs)
3.1. 液晶顯示器原理 (Principle of LCDs)
3.2. TN液晶顯示器 (TN LCDs)
3.3. STN液晶顯示器 (STN LCDs)
3.4.鐵電液晶顯示器 (Ferroelectric LCDs)
3.5. PDLC顯示器 (PDLC Displays)
3.6. TFT液晶顯示器 (TFT LCDs)
3.7. 其他改良型液晶顯示器 (MVA, WVA, IPS LCDs)
4. 液晶顯示相關元件材料及製程 (Device Materials and Process of LCDs)

4.2. 液晶顯示相關元件材料：透明基板 (Substrate)、透明電極 (ITO)、配向層 (Alignment Layer)、間隙物 (Spacer)、彩色濾光片 (Color Filter)、偏光板 (Polarizer)、補償膜 (Compensation Film)、及光源及導光配件 (Backlighting System)

D. 有機發光二極體顯示材料及元件 (OLED and PLED Display Materials and Devices)
1. 有機發光二極體材料基本介紹 (Introduction to OLED and PLED Materials)
1.1. 化學結構 (Chemical Structures)
1.2. 物理性質 (Physical Properties)
2. 有機發光二極體之應用物性與量測 (Physical Properties and Measurements of OLEDs)
3. 有機發光二極體相關原理及元件 (Principle and Devices of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4. 有機發光二極體相關材料及製程 (Device Materials and Process of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4.1. 有機發光二極體製程 (Process of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4.2. 電極基板 (Electrode and Substrate of OLEDs and PLEDs)
4.3. 發光層 (Light-Emitting Layer)
4.4. 電子傳輸層 (Electron Transporting Layer)
4.5. 電洞傳輸層 (Hole Transporting Layer)

E. 有機及高分子太陽能電池材料及元件 (Organic and Polymer Solar Cell Materials and Devices)

cos_cname: 受污染土地和地下水之管理
memo: [English Medium Course]環工所學生優先。
cos_ename: Management of Contaminated Land and Groundwater
crs_outline:
Contamination of land and groundwater is an increasingly serious problem facing environmental and geoenvironmental professionals nowadays. The adverse and harmful impacts of soil and groundwater contamination are long lasting and the environmental damage may even be irreversible. Therefore, proper management of contaminated land and groundwater is vital for the protection of public health and sustainable development of mankind. However, management of contaminated land and groundwater is a complex and multi-disciplinary subject spanning across politics, public administration, socio-economics, sciences etc.
The primary objective of the course is to provide graduate students with exposure to the different facets of contamination management, from prevention to remediation. At the end of the course, the students who fulfill the requirements of this course should be able to understand the importance, considerations, objectives and strategies of contamination management, to delineate subsurface contamination, to quantify the transport and fate of contaminants in the subsurface, to understand available technologies for remediation of contaminated soil and groundwater, and to develop plans for proper management and/or remediation of contaminated land and groundwater.
Each student is required to select a relevant topic of his/her choice to perform independent research and to present his/her findings in a term paper written in English following the format of a scientific journal of his/her choice. The best papers may be invited to present at seminars of the Institute of Environmental Engineering. The term paper will be due at the final examination.

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
This course develops the theoretical foundations of classical and quantum systems away from thermodynamic equilibrium. It begins with stochastic processes and kinetic descriptions, proceeds through linear-response theory, transport, and fluctuation relations, and culminates in hydrodynamics, nonequilibrium phase transitions, field-theoretic methods, and quantum nonequilibrium phenomena.

The central objective is to explain how irreversible macroscopic dynamics, transport, dissipation, and entropy production emerge from microscopic dynamical laws. Particular emphasis is placed on the distinction between equilibrium states, transient nonequilibrium states, and nonequilibrium steady states.

The course is divided into five thematic units:

		-Foundations and stochastic dynamics:
		irreversibility, Markov processes, Langevin dynamics, and Fokker--Planck equations
		
		-Response and transport:
		fluctuation--dissipation relations, kinetic theory, and hydrodynamics
		
		-Nonequilibrium thermodynamics:
		entropy production, steady states, and fluctuation theorems
		
		-Field theory and collective phenomena:
		dynamical path integrals, reaction--diffusion systems, and nonequilibrium phase transitions
		
		-Quantum nonequilibrium physics:
		quantum quenches, equilibration, open systems, Lindblad dynamics, and Keldysh methods

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
In this course, we will go though the basic knowledge and skills to work with biological soft matter.

The 1st part introduces the bio material, including thermotropic liquid crystal, lyotropic liquid crystal, colloids, and biological polymer. We will introduce phase transitions, and demonstrate how to identify the phases and microstucture under microscopes. The electrical, mechanical, and optical properties of the bio soft matter will be discussed, especially, how the structure of the molecule determines the physical properties.

The 2nd part is propagation of light in birefringent material. The birefringence leads to ordinary and extraordinary modes of light propagation, and switches the polarization state of light. The theory will be derived. Additionally, bio materials are chiral materials. They show optical activity. We will investigate how the chirality +  birefringence lead to reflection, transmission, and scattering of light.
This part consist of two art & craft experiments:
(1) Collage of tapes: students will learn how birefringence colors show the orientation of molecules, which is the essential idea of polarized optical microscopy.
(2) Cellulose photonic crystals: it shows the three stable states of chiral liquid crystal, which is the essential idea of colored electronic paper. 

The 3nd part is about the four typical liquid crystal operation modes, which are In-Plane-Switching (IPS), Vertically Aligned (VA), Electrically Controlled Birefringence (ECB), and Twisted Nematic (TN). We will analyze the cell structure, the materials, the assembly, the operation, and their characteristic properties.

Finally we explore the novel bio optoelectronics, such as electronic ink, chromogenic medical reagents, bio electronics and quantum photonics ...etc.


在本課程中，我們會介紹生物物質基本的物理性質，還有如何操作生物光電材料。
第一部分介紹生物材料：熱致型液晶、溶致型液晶、膠體、和生物高分子。我們會介紹物質的相與相變，以及如何用顯微鏡辨識液晶相。我們會討論生物物質的電子、機械、光學性質，以及分子結構如何決定物理性質。

第二部份探討光如何在雙折射物質中傳播。光在雙折射物質中會分解成尋常光與非尋常光，兩種傳播模式的相位差可以用來切換光的偏極態。生物物質還有手性(旋光性)，我們會繼續討論手性結構如何造成旋光穿透/反射/散射。
此部份做兩個美勞實驗：
(1)膠帶拼貼畫：體驗如何用雙折射色判斷分子指向(偏光顯微術的基本原理)。
(2)纖維素光子晶體：體驗手性液晶三穩態(彩色電子紙的基本原理)。

第三部分介紹四種典型的液晶(向列型物質)的操作模式，分別是水平操作模式(IPS)、垂直操作模式(VA)、電控雙折射模式(ECB)和扭轉操作模式(TN)。我們將分析元件的結構、材料、如何組裝、如何操作及其特性。

最後我們探討新穎生物光電元件，例如：電子墨水、顯色式醫學試片、生物電子 / 光量子元件...等等。
