memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
The physical world, from the behavior of electrons in solids to the structure of atomic nuclei and the properties of quantum fluids, is fundamentally governed by the interactions between a vast number of constituent particles. While single-particle descriptions provide a crucial starting point, they typically fall short in capturing the rich physics of collective phenomena and emergent properties that arise solely from these interactions. Phenomena such as superconductivity, magnetism, the fractional quantum Hall effect, and the properties of strongly correlated materials cannot be understood without a theoretical framework capable of addressing the complex interplay of many interacting degrees of freedom.

The course "Many-Body Physics" provides a formal introduction to the theoretical tools and conceptual frameworks necessary for describing interacting systems that underlie much of modern condensed matter physics, quantum chemistry, nuclear physics, and even aspects of high-energy physics.

Methodologically, the course is built around the path integral approach to many-body physics. 
Rather than developing operator-based perturbation theory as the primary tool, we will formulate the many-body problem in terms of functional integrals over coherent states of bosonic and fermionic (Grassmann) fields. This perspective offers a unified language in which the quantum mechanics of interacting systems and their statistical mechanics at finite temperature appear on equal footing, connected simply by a Wick rotation to imaginary time. The path integral formalism provides a natural and systematic route to perturbation theory and Feynman diagrams, to the treatment of symmetries and their spontaneous breaking, to mean-field and saddle-point approximations via the identification of stationary field configurations, and to the study of collective fluctuations through the expansion of the action beyond the saddle point. It also furnishes the most direct bridge to renormalization group ideas and to the effective field theory description of low-energy, long-wavelength physics — techniques that will recur throughout the course and that are indispensable in the contemporary research literature.

This course serves as a crucial bridge between foundational quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics and the advanced topics encountered in contemporary research literature and specialized fields.

This course is a journal club for the Polymer Science group, designed to train students to independently read and present polymer science literature. In the first part of the semester, students each select a paper and present it individually in class, followed by open discussion and questions. Near the end of the semester, the class carries out a single peer-review exercise in which students use generative AI tools to help produce a report, verify its content themselves, and then have it reviewed by classmates, with the instructor arbitrating any disputed points. The course builds skills in literature reading, oral presentation, and — in an era of AI-assisted research and writing — the verification and peer-review judgment needed to work responsibly with generative AI

The latter half of the course focuses on predicting the kinetics of polymerization reactions, connecting theoretical methods to real polymer chemistry problems.

crs_outline:
Photonic technologies are indispensable experimental tools in modern physical chemistry and many interdisciplinary fields, including biomedicine, materials science, and nanotechnology. This course is designed for graduate students and advanced undergraduate students interested in applying photonic techniques to scientific research.
The course adopts a bottom-up approach. It begins at the component level, introducing the fundamentals of optics, optical and optomechanical components, light sources, and photodetectors. It then progresses to the system level, where these components are integrated into representative photonic instruments used in physical chemistry. Finally, real research setups are presented to illustrate how photonic systems are designed and implemented in the laboratory.
By the end of the course, students will understand the operating principles of modern photonic instruments and be able to relate individual optical components to complete experimental systems used in scientific research.

crs_outline:
Laser Chemistry is a graduate-level course that provides an advanced introduction to the principles and applications of lasers in chemistry. The course focuses on the interaction between light and matter, laser spectroscopy, photochemical and photophysical processes, and laser-based methods for probing and controlling molecular and material systems.

The course will cover both fundamental concepts and selected advanced topics, including molecular spectroscopy, reaction dynamics, nonlinear optical processes, laser-induced heating, optical trapping, laser-induced crystallization, and laser-based manipulation of soft matter and molecular assemblies. Through lectures, discussions, and examples from recent research, students will learn how laser techniques are applied to investigate chemical structures, molecular dynamics, reaction mechanisms, and materials processes.

Course Objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

Explain the fundamental principles of lasers and laser–matter interactions.
Understand the theoretical basis and practical applications of laser spectroscopy.
Describe photochemical and photophysical processes induced by laser irradiation.
Discuss how lasers can be used to probe, control, and manipulate molecular and material systems.
Critically evaluate recent research examples involving laser chemistry, laser trapping, laser-induced crystallization, and related phenomena.
Apply concepts of laser chemistry to their own research fields in chemistry, materials science, photochemistry, and related areas.

cos_cname: 可信任人工智慧：統計機器學習與最佳化
memo: [English Medium Course]
cos_ename: Trustworthy AI: Statistical Machine Learning and Optimization
crs_outline:
This course centers on Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (TAI) and integrates methods from statistical machine learning and optimization to examine challenges faced by AI systems in real-world applications, including interpretability, uncertainty, reliability, and decision quality. The course guides students to understand, from the perspectives of data, models, decision-making, and deployment, that AI models should not only pursue predictive accuracy but also be understandable, verifiable, correctable, and capable of supporting robust decisions in complex and changing environments.

Topics include foundational concepts of trustworthy AI, explainable AI, uncertainty quantification, and data-driven decision-making and optimization. Through homework assignments, paper reading, oral presentations, and a final project, students will learn to analyze limitations of AI systems, select and design appropriate statistical machine learning and optimization methods, and translate analyses into practically meaningful or research-relevant models, evidence, and decision recommendations.

After completing this course, students will be able to:
- Understand core concepts of trustworthy AI, statistical machine learning, and optimization, and apply them appropriately to data analysis, model evaluation, and decision-support problems.
- Analyze trustworthy AI issues such as interpretability, uncertainty, and reliability, and evaluate their impacts on model usage and decision quality.
- Develop the ability to read academic papers, structure problems, and communicate research ideas clearly on trustworthy-AI-related topics.
- Integrate statistical machine learning, optimization, and application contexts to design new analytical methods or validation procedures, and present effectiveness and limitations in a project format.

Course learning goals include:
- Critical thinking: Understand the systemic nature of trustworthy AI problems, application contexts, and sources of risk.
- Research skills: Learn how to search for, read, organize, and critique trustworthy AI literature.
- Integrative skills: Design new methods and validation pipelines, and clearly explain advantages, limitations, and applicable scenarios.

Course Scope:
This course does not aim to comprehensively cover all modern AI topics, such as LLMs, computer vision, VLMs, reinforcement learning, or agentic AI. Instead, it mainly approaches trustworthy AI from the perspectives of statistical machine learning, uncertainty quantification, explainability, reliability, and optimization-based decision-making. However, final project topics are open-ended and may involve any AI-related application, as long as they address trustworthy AI issues.

本課程以可信任人工智慧為核心，結合統計機器學習與最佳化方法，探討人工智慧系統在真實應用場域中所面臨的可解釋性、不確定性、可靠性、與決策品質等議題。課程引導學生從資料、模型、決策與系統部署的角度，理解 AI 模型不只是追求預測準確率，也必須能被理解、被檢驗、被修正，並在複雜且變動的環境中支援穩健決策。

課程內容涵蓋可信任 AI 的基本概念、可解釋人工智慧、不確定性量化、資料驅動決策與最佳化等主題。學生將透過作業、論文閱讀、口頭報告與專題實作，學習如何分析 AI 系統的限制，選擇與設計合適的統計機器學習與最佳化方法，並將分析結果轉化為具實務意義或研究價值的模型、證據與決策建議。

修習本課程後，學生將能夠：
- 掌握可信任 AI、統計機器學習與最佳化的基本概念，並能正確應用於資料分析、模型評估與決策支援問題。
- 理解可解釋性、不確定性、分佈變動與模型更新等可信任 AI 議題，並能評估其對模型使用與決策品質的影響。
- 培養學術論文閱讀、問題整理與研究表達能力，能針對可信任 AI 相關主題提出清楚的研究觀點。
- 整合統計機器學習、最佳化與應用情境，設計新的分析方法或驗證流程，並以專題形式呈現其有效性與限制。

本課程的學習目標，包含：
- 思辨能力：理解可信任 AI 問題的系統性、應用脈絡與風險來源。
- 研究能力：學習如何搜尋、閱讀、整理與評論可信任 AI 相關論文。
- 整合型能力：設計新方法、建立驗證流程，並能清楚說明方法的優點、限制與適用情境。

課程範圍：
本課程並非旨在完整涵蓋所有現代人工智慧主題，例如大型語言模型、電腦視覺、視覺語言模型、強化學習或 Agentic AI。相較之下，本課程主要從統計機器學習、不確定性量化、可解釋性、可靠性，以及以最佳化為基礎的決策制定等角度切入可信任人工智慧。期末專題主題採開放形式，可涵蓋任何 AI 相關應用；但專題內容需回應可信任人工智慧相關議題。

crs_outline: Stochastic thermodynamics extends classical thermodynamics to individual fluctuating trajectories of small systems, such as colloidal particles, molecular motors, proteins, cells, quantum dots, single-electron transistors, and cold atoms. While classical thermodynamics focuses on average quantities like energy, heat, work, and entropy, stochastic thermodynamics accounts for strong thermal fluctuations at microscopic scales, treating quantities such as heat and work as random variables that vary from one trajectory to another. Information thermodynamics further extends this framework by explicitly incorporating information as a physical quantity that can be quantified, manipulated, and converted into energetic costs or gains. The goal of this course is to equip students with the skills needed to analyze and solve problems involving such small systems across these diverse physical settings.

crs_outline:
Introduction to Electrodynamics (ED).
Few theories have been as formative for the development of modern science as classical electrodynamics. Formulated in the late 1800’s and refined in the early 1900’s to this day it forms the solid basis of most day-to-day physics phenomena we observe and use in our technologies. In this course we will study ED from its inception in Maxwell’s equations and develop it towards its covariant formulation. Along the way we will encounter and solve problems in Electro-/Magnetostatics, Radiation Theory, ED in Matter, Electromagnetic Waves and the Lagrangian formulation of classical field theories.

crs_outline:
Lattice gauge theory (LGT) represents one of the most powerful and advanced formalisms in science to study the most fundamental dynamics of atomic and sub-atomic systems. It has applications that range from condensed matter to particle theory, from the study of phase transitions to quantum scattering.

In this course we will learn the formalism to address the physics of systems that interact via the exchange of gauge bosons. These are called Yang-Mills theories and we will discuss them both with Abelian and non-Abelian gauge groups. Expanding our findings to theories that also include scalar particles we will study the physics of the Higgs boson in the Standard Model. By pushing even further and adding in fermions we will finally arrive at a fully non-perturbative description of quantum chromodynamics, the theory of the strong force. 

Our research will lead us to the realisation that a full result requires the numerical simulation of the system on a (super-)computer and we will practice how to perform such simulations. In addition we will learn how to derive meaningful physics results that cannot be obtained any other way. Throughout emphasis is put on practical implementations.

During the course we will develop codes for:
- The bootstrap resampling and fitting of data with a linear ansatz
- The simulation of the Ising Model using a Heatbath algorithm
- The simulation of scalar field theory using the Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm
- Inversion of a fermion matrix using the Conjugate Gradient algorithm

memo: 初選第三階段起，限管科系研究所學生選修。※管科系、資財系大二學生限修大學部財務管理課程。※管院學生(含雙主修、輔系、跨域學程)若有特殊原因須修習此研究所課程抵免大學部財務管理課程之學分，須於修課前向所屬系辦申請，並經由此課程召集老師同意始得認列學分。陽明校區欲加選可寫E-mail給老師，謝謝。
crs_outline:
1.期中考階段從基礎財務管理理論出發，搭配板書示範與講授財務實務資料，介紹報酬、風險、事件研究、房地產投資的理論基礎。接著，本課程闡釋財務管理資本資產定價理論，培養同學資本資產評價的實力，課程進行中，老師提供國家考試高考或證券投資顧問事業證券投資分析人員相關試題，分析學生畢業後，財務管理就業與考試趨勢分析，老師進而板書解題示範引導作答方向，學生從做中學領悟投資意涵，幫助學生建立財務管理的基本觀念。
2.期末報告階段老師循序漸進引導學生實作事件研究，奠定投資實務與學術論文撰寫基礎，進行財務與人工智慧的跨域教學，強調財務、產業分析和人工智慧跨域學習，釐清人工智慧深入影響各種產業，投資人選擇投資標的應考量人工智慧，才能有效衡量公司價值，避免錯估企業的成效與價值，課程進行中老師也會穿插真實的案例實際教導同學實務上財務管理的運作。
3.課程安排的學術論文，從永續發展文獻可看出財務管理課程因應全球永續發展目標的潮流，教導學生投資標的需順勢選取致力綠色製程與綠色產品創新的企業(諸如台積電等)，投資選股前事先參考會計師認證的「永續發展、社會責任暨公司治理報告書」，判別企業的綠色績效，選擇前景良好的公司進行投資，提升長期投資的獲益。
4.本課程以財務學出發，帶學生領悟實務界預測公司股價的基礎，以數學證明的方式，讓學生了解證券金融產業每股盈餘比率(本益比)設定在20的理論基礎，以利同學投資理財之應用，理論與實務結合。

crs_outline: Strategic management is concerned with managing the competitive position (including the general environment, industry and market structure, and organizational strengths and weaknesses) and long-term development of the business enterprise. This course aims to relate the principles and issues addressed in the various functional business areas to introduce an integrated concept of management and provide an understanding of the relationship between theory and practice in general management. The course will lead students into two main areas which must be analyzed in order to formulate and implement a well-conceived strategy: the external environment of the firm (the industry context), and the internal environment of the firm (its resources and capabilities). Some of the key topics covered include: (1) exploring why and how good strategic management increases business performance, (2) the application of a set of analytical frameworks, (3) analyzing the reasons for the success and failure of a firm, and (4) the methods of developing an effective competitive strategy and executing it competently. The teaching materials include lectures, case analyses, and independent readings.

crs_outline: This course is designed to develop graduate students’ academic research and scholarly writing skills in the field of global business. The course provides systematic guidance on the process of conducting academic research, including identifying research questions, reviewing and synthesizing literature, developing theoretical frameworks, designing research methodologies, analyzing data, and writing academic papers suitable for conference presentations and journal submissions. Through readings of high-quality journal articles, discussions of research design, writing workshops, and academic projects, students will learn how to critically evaluate existing research and contribute to scholarly conversations in global business. Particular emphasis is placed on academic writing, argument development, theoretical contribution, and research ethics. By the end of the course, students will be able to develop a research proposal and produce a well-structured academic paper that meets the standards of graduate-level research.

crs_outline:
Course Description:
This course introduces financial accounting steps by steps to students. Accounting involves the entire process of identifying, recording and communicating business events. First of all, this course interprets accounting principles, ethics and the role of accounting in business environments. Next, we instruct students to employ information of accounting statements to assess corporate financial status, operation achievements and cash flows. Another feature of this course is to lead students to understand accounting process and to teach them accounting practices such as agency problems and earnings management, so as to spark students’ interests in accounting. Our study of accounting will provide students insight into financial statement analysis, so students can successfully uncover business questions through analyzing accounting information.

Objectives/Goals:
Students in this course can learn following issues. 
1.  Understand the basic accounting principles and assumptions of recording enterprise transactions.
2.  Realize the procedure of the accounting cycle from entry journals, T-accounts to the preparation of accounting statements.
3.  Prepare income statements, statements of financial position, and cash flow statement. 
4.  Learn about current issues that the accounting field is concerned about, such as expected credit loss and gain, research development, and further discuss present controversies of accounting standards.
5.  Realize accounting practices and analyze financial statements through case studies.

專題研討課程分為上、下二學期，並以同學輪流上台簡報、主持及參與提問與討論之方式進行。上學期以研讀並報告與同學論文主題相關之國內外文獻(Key Paper)為主，下學期則報告同學碩士論文之研究內容、執行進度與階段性成果為主。

學生完成本課程（上學期專題研討）後，應能夠：
1.	依據自身論文主題，選擇與研究方向相關之國內外核心文獻，並清楚說明該文獻之研究問題、研究方法、分析流程、主要成果與研究限制。
2.	透過 Key Paper 研讀，理解相關領域常用之研究設計、資料處理方式、分析方法與結果呈現方式，並作為後續碩士論文研究設計之參考。
3.	針對報告內容提出問題與回饋，並透過研討過程理解文獻內容、掌握問題核心及參與學術討論。
4.	主持專題研討活動，掌握研討會流程、時間控管、引導提問與討論及串場安排，並展現主持學術活動及會場互動之能力。
5.	透過文獻報告與討論，使與會同儕了解彼此的研究問題、研究方向與參考文獻，並建立後續研究交流、合作及專業交流網絡之基礎。

It includes the following topics: C++ / Python language tutorial, data structures, elementary and advanced searching & sorting algorithms, graph algorithms (Dijkstra's Algorithm, Augmenting Path algorithm, Prim's Algorithm, Kruskal's Algorithm, etc.) and algorithm design techniques (Divide-and-Conquer Algorithms, Dynamic Programming, Branch-and-Bound Technique, Meta-Heuristics). After taking the course, students are expected to be able to solve transportation problems using computer algorithms with C++/ Python language.

The main theme is to emphasize the applications of risk management concepts and principles to transportation planning, operation, control, and management. The first half of this course will be discussing the fundamental aspects of risk management, including the basic concepts, principles, and applications for operational and safety risks. The second half will be focusing on transportation risk management-related research and modeling. crs_outline:
We live inside systems: hospitals, semiconductor supply chains, drone delivery networks, traffic infrastructure, and many others. None of these are built by one expert or one discipline. They are built by teams who must agree on what the system should do, who it serves, what situations it must handle, and how every part connects, behaves, and is verified. That disciplined agreement — structured, traceable, and tested against reality — is what systems engineering exists to produce.
This course begins with a simple question: what is a system? A system is not only a collection of parts. It is defined by boundaries, relationships, interfaces, behaviors, constraints, and emergent outcomes. Learning to see these connections is the foundation of systems thinking. We will study systems engineering as both a technical discipline and a leadership discipline. Systems engineers help teams clarify stakeholder needs, define Use Cases, resolve conflicts, evaluate trade-offs, control changes, and turn complex intentions into buildable and verifiable designs.
In the AI era, this discipline becomes even more important. Large language models and agentic AI tools can accelerate development, but they also require stronger judgment, traceability, verification, and human ownership. Specifications may evolve faster, but change still must be controlled. Systems may become more adaptive, but safety and accountability cannot be lost.  In this course, you will first learn traditional document-based systems engineering: CONOPS, Use Cases, requirements, functional architecture, interfaces, verification plans, and traceability matrices. You will then move into Model-Based Systems Engineering, or MBSE, where interconnected models make system structure, behavior, requirements, Use Cases, interfaces, and verification logic more visible and consistent.
Students will also use AI-assisted tools to support modeling and documentation, while learning to audit, question, and own what those tools produce. By the end of this semester, you will not only know about systems engineering. You will have practiced it — from stakeholder needs and Use Cases to a connected, traceable, and verifiable system design. The goal is to help students think like a systems engineer in the AI era.

cos_ename: Design and Practice of Generative AI Systems
dep_ename: Department of Industrial Engineering and Management
crs_outline:
本課程聚焦於生成式 AI 在企業場域中的系統化設計與實務應用，課程內容從大型語言模型基礎出發，延伸至檢索增強生成（RAG）、Agentic Workflow、智能體系統、小型語言模型（SLM）部署，以及 SDD / TDD 導向的 AI 系統架構設計。
本課程不以單純操作生成式 AI 工具為目標，而是引導學生理解如何將語言模型整合至企業資料、流程、工具與資訊系統中，設計出可測試、可評估、可維護且具備實際落地價值的 AI 應用。
修課學生完成本課程後，應能：
○ 說明企業級生成式 AI 系統的基本架構，包括前端、後端、資料庫、向量庫、模型、API、權限與紀錄追蹤。
○ 建置可驗證的 RAG 系統，完成文件切分、Metadata 設計、Embedding、向量檢索、回答生成與來源引用。
○ 設計可使用工具、呼叫 API、查詢資料庫與執行流程的 Agent / 智能體工作流。
○ 比較 LLM、SLM、地端模型與雲端模型在成本、延遲、資料安全與維運上的取捨。
○ 運用 SDD / TDD 思維撰寫 AI 系統規格、測試案例與驗收標準。
○ 完成一個具備資料檢索、工具呼叫、流程控制、測試驗證與部署規劃的企業 AI 系統原型。

cos_ename: Algorithmic Mechanism Design and Social Choice
dep_ename: Institute of Hospital and Health Care Administration
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
Algorithmic game theory and learning sprouts as an active interdisciplinary field integrating computer science and economics. While its impacting contributions, namely, the efficiency of equilibria and complexity of computing equilibria are more on the measurement and analysis side of equilibria, treating equilibria as an engineerable aggregated choice, “algorithmic mechanism design and social choice” which is more on the engineering side also develops promisingly in parallel and produces lots of interesting and well-unknown results. Based on the classical results in mechanism design and social choice in economics, our goals are introducing various mechanism design questions and topics from computational and algorithmic perspectives, complementary to  algorithmic game theory and learning.

crs_outline: 本課程提供金融機構運作與管理之基本知識，討論各類金融機構在金融市場之角色與營業模式，提供同學未來於金融機構業求職的參考與背景知識。課程內容分析商業銀行、投資銀行、保險公司、證券商、共同基金、租賃公司等金融機構之基本運作邏輯、獲利模式，並強調金融機構風險管理，涵蓋市場風險、利率風險、信用風險、流動性風險、及作業風險之衡量與管理。內容並連結近期金融海嘯的重大衝擊，分析其成因、影響、和後續變化，包括資產負債表外項目、證券化等因素的對市場的影響。課程中也會討論金融科技的新趨勢。

Students will engage in hands-on projects—shared via GitHub—that integrate theoretical concepts with practical programming. The course centers on solving real-world problems in FinTech, encouraging collaboration, innovation, and data-driven decision-making.

In addition to technical skills, students will enhance their oral presentation abilities and learn to leverage tools like ChatGPT to improve their coding and writing. Team projects will focus on key FinTech applications such as credit scoring, fraud detection, factor investing in Taiwan’s stock market, and cryptocurrency trading.

To facilitate the course, students are required to:
1) Bring a laptop to every lecture.
2) Create free accounts on the following platforms: GitHub, Overleaf, and Microsoft Teams (using their NYCU accounts).

dep_ename: Department of Information and Finance Management
crs_outline:
本課程教主要教授人工智慧、機器學習的理論與實務，並延伸至深度學習的基礎知識，包含Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) 和 Long-short term memory network (LSTM)等的架構與實作教學，此外對於近年來蓬勃發展的金融科技領域，也將從資財系的觀點提供資工、資管、財金或其他相關科系的研究生，踏入CS+Finance跨領域學習的必備基礎，這門課程將包含大量的Python程式實作，也會在金融投資、衍生性商品訂價、電腦視覺、數據資料分析多個實務應用中，藉由上機實作教學、課堂程式作業、小組合作專題、報告與討論各種方式，讓所有學生具備跨足人工智慧、機器學習、金融科技等所需的資訊技術與應用領域知識，課程內容包含：
1.	機器學習理論：以人工智慧、統計理論實作、樣型辨識模型與機器學習理論相關的知識為主，概述各種演算法，諸如：Concept Learning、Decision Tree、Artificial Neural Networks、Genetic Algorithms、Support Vector Machines、Instance-based Learning、Clustering Analysis、AdaBoost algorithm
2.	實例應用系統開發：在大數據分析及決策的各種跨領域應用中，以多媒體與財務資料庫較易取得，故依修課同學背景分成多媒體系統決策與財務投資決策兩組，多媒體組以大量影像、聲音、影片資訊為研究標的，探討諸如人臉偵測、人臉辨識、智慧人機互動、人體姿勢模型等先進智慧型影像識別技術及其應用。而財務投資決策則將所學之人工智慧與機器學習理論，應用於財務時間序列中，並藉此探討各種創新金融與財務管理議題。
本課程除了學習人工智慧與深度學習理論，另藉由實例應用開發來建構同學們實作的能力。此外，雙應用主題的課程設計將有效協助不同研究背景的同學，快速達到學以致用的目的。期望能將各種已經成熟的AI科技，推展至各種管理決策與產品創新應用的電腦化與智慧化。

dep_ename: Department of Information and Finance Management
crs_outline:
1.  This is the class about the valuation of an investment project or a company.
2.  The course first reviews the traditional discounted-cash-flow (DCF) or net-present-value (NPV) methods. 
3.  This class then introduces some real-options concepts to value an investment project or a company. This new approach is called an expanded NPV method.
4.  Finally, some basic game-theory concepts will be further employed into the expanded NPV method to consider the strategic action by competitors.
5.  By introducing lots of numerical examples, practical cases and applications, this course will train students and provide them the ability to value an investment project or a company by themselves.
6. Lecture will be provided in Chinese.

企業從事合併與收購以追求外部成長，其必須結合公司理財、證券市場、策略管理、財務會計與財經法律的知識與人才，因此合併與收購所承擔的風險並不亞於內部成長。本課程以公司理財（Corporate Finance）理論為基礎，並且強化購併個案介紹和評述，以及公司評價模型的分析。課程內容包含：購併程序、風險管理、個案分析、due diligence、購併策略、公司評價、接管與反接管措施。

crs_outline: Some complicated data involving relationships can be represented as a graph that consists of nodes and edges between nodes. Such graphs can serve as a fundamental tool for modeling social, technological, and biological systems. This course focuses on the computational, algorithmic, and modeling challenges specific to the analysis of massive graphs. By means of studying the underlying graph structure and its features, students are introduced to machine learning techniques and data mining tools that can help us to reveal insights into a variety of networks. We will focus on representation learning and Graph Neural Networks. Furthermore, we will cover algorithms for the World Wide Web, influence maximization, disease outbreak detection, and social network analysis.

crs_outline:
科學技術創新的進步是如此地快速, 人類的反應和適應力, 社會和道德、經濟和企業、政治和法規等等都跟不上腳步, 時間一久, 全都亂了套, 到底 ”科技創新” 要將人類帶往何處? 這門課就要探討這個問題。
夲課的重點是給予學生近十年內最新的科技創新發展和對人類歷史發展的新看法。希望學生在認知上能有所啟發、探索、思考、判斷、選擇和為什麼。大學研究所的教育在於強化學生深入分析批判、綜合思考、創新思維且擁有清晰表達自己理念的能力，使他們終身受益、擁有最寶貴的技能。 
所以這門課的重點在於學生勇於表達自己的想法和問題。基本上夲課要求學生:平時的出席率、課堂Quizzes上寫出自己的看法和參與課堂上的討論。 
夲課程聚焦在最新的科技創新和知識的更新, 領域包括半導體、無線通訊、物聯網、車聯網、自動化、中美貿易科技戰、AI人工智慧、人體醫學、地球暖化、人類發展史等方向, 每方向將會選擇一些相關子題來探討。
本學期的重點放在：科技管理、人類發展史、中美貿易戰：半導體產業及A I人工智慧發展、人體醫學。

crs_outline: The intent of this course aims to effectively address the pattern recognition problems of smart healthcare data by developing high performance machine learning models. In the 21th century, the medical data are generated by a variety of elaborated medical diagnostic machines, and these medical data are usually complicated with the uncertainty. Through addressing the pattern recognition problem of medical data, the pattern or hidden information can be positively discovered from medical raw data, and it can further bring a good diversity of contribution to smart healthcare, such as key symptom identification and clinical decision support. Through giving a brief concept of machine learning modeling, this also provides real works to accumulate the practical experience of addressing the pattern recognition problem of smart healthcare data. Upon completion of this course, students will have the rudimentary knowledge of machine learning and the corresponding skills to address the pattern recognition problem of smart healthcare data.

crs_outline:
This course aims to analyze technology management literature by first-principle approach. Academic papers are deconstructed into systematic components, e.g. external Environment, literature analysis leading to the argument, what is the problem? what is literature gap? what does this research contribute to the scholarly literature by addressing the problem, etc. The deconstruction of research paper is associated with subsequent reconstruction process to develop new knowledge.

The objective of this course is to help student build up a reservoir of “first principles” in technology management and associate those principles with different fields. Students can learn how to deconstruct knowledge into fundamental principles then reconstruct the fundamental principles in new fields to facilitate efficient learning transfer and knowledge recombination.

• Explain the main theories about creativity and its cultivation. 
• Illustrate the creative and innovation processes. 
• Apply appropriate creativity tools for problem-solving. 
• Collaborate with cross-disciplinary students and develop a creative solution that solves real problems.

The course includes lectures, in-class discussions and exercises, games, field visits, learning reflections, readings, presentations, and project writing.

本課程為陽明交大管理學院多位教授與台積電(TSMC)多位主管合作開授之課程。課程以全球觀點介紹半導體產業重要管理議題。課程由陽明交大管理學院教授們與台積電主管們共同授課，開放管院碩博士班學生(不含在職專班學生)選課。課程結合理論與實務，學生也將在課程中學習世界一流的半導體公司台積電第一手的經營管理實務。課程將提供學生以下知識：

crs_outline:
當前全球面臨社會不平等加劇、科技發展帶來的倫理與治理挑戰，以及永續發展壓力，如何透過創新治理機制促進更公平且負責任的科技發展，已成為學術界與政策制定者關注的核心議題。本課程聚焦於負責任創新（Responsible Innovation, RI）、區域創新(Regional Innovation)與包容導向創新（Inclusive Innovation）的理論與實踐，培養學生對科技發展與社會變遷的理解及應用能力。課程內容導入包容導向創新、聯合國永續發展目標（Sustainable Development Goals, SDGs）、以及負責任創新的核心概念，透過探索式教學場域，讓學生深入理解科技治理的挑戰與可能解方。本課程不僅關注科技創新的社會影響，也探討政策規範、企業治理、社會責任及創新生態系統的建構，使學生能夠理解如何透過科技與創新實踐促進社會可持續發展。本課程將從負責任創新的理論基礎出發，參考英國研究與創新局（UK Research and Innovation, UKRI）所定義的負責任創新AREA架構，包括預期（Anticipate）、反思（Reflect）、參與（Engage）、行動（Act）。透過系統化的研究方法與實務應用，學生將學習如何在科技創新與社會發展的交互作用中納入永續社會責任考量，分析科技創新可能帶來的影響，探索其在經濟、社會、治理等層面的變遷，並透過開放對話與多元利害關係人的參與機制，設計出能夠回應社會需求的創新方案。
The primary objectives of this course include training in key research methods in the field of technology management and an in-depth review of important theoretical and practical literature in technology innovation management. A particular focus is placed on understanding and applying responsible innovation to design solutions that address diverse societal needs, thereby enhancing the fairness and accessibility of technological applications. The course will build upon the theoretical foundations of responsible innovation, drawing on the UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) definition of responsible innovation through the AREA framework: Anticipate, Reflect, Engage, and Act. By integrating systematic research methods with practical applications, students will learn to incorporate social responsibility considerations into technology innovation management. The course will guide students in analyzing the potential impacts of technological innovations, exploring their possible economic, social, and environmental consequences while emphasizing open dialogue and stakeholder engagement throughout the research and innovation process.

crs_outline:
人工智慧的突破性發展，不僅對人類社會產生前所未有的衝擊，也對既有法律概念及制度造成史無前例的挑戰。在技術快速發展下，法律面應該如何加以規範? 藉由人工智慧而生的產出物，究應由誰擁有智慧財產權？無人車肇事誰應負責？人工智慧對法律服務業會造成何種衝擊？機器人會犯罪嗎？本課程檢視國內外既有文獻及案例，為學習者提供清楚的議題藍圖及深度分析。本課程在授課內容上分三大部分: (1) 人工智慧相關之法律規範，(2) 人工智慧技術在法律領域之運用，(3) 針對重要主題由不同老師深入剖析。

在課程目標方面，藉由課程及討論，同學應能掌握技術面及法制面的基本概念，並進一步探討案例及適用法規。在現今社會整體科技快速發展下，法律背景的同學除須具備法律素養外，更應具備接納新知、研讀、吸收的能力，理工醫背景的同學亦可藉由此課程熟悉法律制度，在發展技術的同時，兼顧法律及倫理議題，並藉由案例判讀、期末報告撰寫的過程，培養對跨領域議題批判思考的能力。

cos_ename: Civil Law: General Provisions of Obligations
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
民法乃法律人必備的基本功，若地基打得好，無論目標是往上加蓋多少樓層，或興建任何式樣新穎的房子，都可輕鬆達成，事半功倍。因此，凡法律人，不分專精領域為何，民法均乃必修課目。債總是學習民法者必須打通的任督二脈，無論是法定之債或是意定之債，熟知法條操作的基礎以及準用或類推適用法條的原理原則，均有助於法律邏輯的推論以及強化認事用法的能力。本課程目的除了教授學生如何從市場經濟主導下的契約自由原則出發，熟稔各種債的基本原理原則之外，亦希望隨著課堂上對法律概念的介紹、實例題的演練，引導同學反覆推敲如何將一個複雜的法律事實濃縮爭點，將之由繁化簡，並透過三段論法以及請求權基礎解答法，將所有可能存在的債法問題逐一破解。
主要課程內容：
1. 契約法之重要概念。
2. 侵權行為法之重要概念。
3. 其他法定債之關係的重要概念。
學習目標：
1. 理解債法之基本內涵。
2. 運用債法之各項規定。
3. 分析重要的實務議題。
預期學習成果：
1.	掌握債法之基本內涵並能適用於具體事實之中，針對債法議題作出詳盡之法律分析。
2.	具備閱讀法院判決與分析其法律意見之利益。

crs_outline:
Course Description:
This course offers a dynamic and immersive international negotiation simulation. Participants will be organized into two teams, with students representing one of two companies. These teams will explore a partnership to harness the potential of a groundbreaking new element, Changesium, which promises to revolutionize the speed of semiconductor chips. The collaboration may take various forms, including a joint venture, licensing agreement, or long-term supply contract, among possible arrangements. Engagements will occur through a mix of written communications and live negotiations, offering a practical experience of the negotiation process.
The primary goal of this course is to provide a realistic experience of business negotiations. Students will be required to dedicate time outside the classroom to strategize with their team, prepare for discussions that revolve around email exchanges, and gear up for the negotiation sessions. Classroom discussions will delve into negotiation strategies, progress updates, and the examination of legal, business, and policy considerations that influence the negotiations. By participating in this simulation, students will gain valuable insights into the complexities of cross-business negotiations, enhancing their practical negotiation skills in a global context.

Course Objectives:
Upon completion of this course, an engaged student will be able to:
•	Conduct an interest-based negotiation.
•	Plan an effective strategy for negotiation that includes
o	Assessing the client’s position, by identifying the client’s interests, BATNA, Reservation Point, and Target Point.
o	Assessing the other party’s position, by estimating the party’s interests, BATNA, Reservation Point, and Target Point.
o	Estimating a Zone of Possible Agreement (ZOPA).
o	Assessing additional factors surrounding the negotiation (including cultural context, political situations, economic situation, industry, labor issues, and capital infrastructure).
o	Identifying the negotiation issues (conflicting interests between the parties). 
o	Bundling issues in multi-issue negotiations.
o	Preparing an opening offer or responding to an offer.
•	Draft and properly time written communications, professional and appropriate in tone, to the other party.
•	Assess one’s own negotiation style and employ methods to strengthen weaknesses. Recognize and aptly respond to the other party’s negotiation style.
•	Determine and communicate a reasonable opening offer that maximizes value to your client. Adeptly respond to an opening offer.
•	Skillfully gather information from the other party and strategically reveal your client’s information to the other party.
•	Identify ethical issues and respond appropriately.
•	Employ appropriate blocking techniques to avoid answering certain questions.
•	Respond appropriately to surprise information.
•	Make properly timed principled concessions.
•	Distribute value between the parties.
•	Effectively employ strategies to move beyond counter-productive emotions and impasse.
•	Recognize when to walk away from a deal.
•	Conduct a post-negotiation evaluation.

crs_outline:
本課程著重於跨領域學習並分兩個主軸: 

* Track A 協助法律人掌握資訊科技的重要基礎概念

* Track B 透過資訊科技應在法律領域培養實作能力

Track A 將以 CS50 for Lawyers (哈佛大學針對法律系學生設計之 Computer Science 入門課程) 為主，解說重要基礎概念如: Computational Thinking, Programming Languages, Algorithms, Data Structures, Cryptography, Cybersecurity, Internet Technologies, Cloud Computing, Web Development, Database Design, Cybersecurity, etc. 課堂上將透過同學們事先提問的問題，協助非技術背景同學建立對資訊科技的直觀理解，以便日後面對科技相關法律案件時，具備相當程度的掌握能力。

Track B 將透過 CS50P (Programming with Python) 建立初步程式設計概念，並補充說明人工智慧領域的應用，協助同學在資訊科技最基礎與最新發展兩端，都能有所認識並思考應用於法律領域的各種可能。

預期同學之學習成果：
1. 能掌握資訊科技之基礎知識與人工智慧之發展動態。
2. 能就技術本質深入思考與資訊科技相關的法律議題。
3. 能認識 LegalTech 應用潛力並培養實作能力。
4. 期末專題針對 Track A 或 Track B 擇一研究。

cos_cname: 國際商務仲裁實例演練
memo: [English Medium Course]限科法所同學選修
crs_outline:
The course is designed to train lawyering skills through moot court training based on and/or participation in Annual Willem C. Vis (East) international Commercial Arbitration Moot competition. Traditional legal education does not provide adequate training on lawyering skills, such as research, legal argumentation, legal persuasive writing, as well as efficient and effective oral communications with the adjudicating tribunals. This course intends to fill the gap. Through the course students will understand the functions and practices of international commercial arbitral tribunals. In addition, students will be required to conduct research, to write written submissions, and to present oral arguments through teamwork. Students will, accordingly, acquire essential skills necessary for the career of international lawyer.
Accordingly, the core of the course is to train advocacy ability of the students. The emphasis is thus not on legal rules. Instead, the focus of the teaching will be on the writing and oral abilities. The actual content of the course will be adjusted according to the Vis Moot problem of the year. There will be no lectures in the class. Instead, the course will focus on exercises of legal research, legal writing, and oral presentation skills. Students are expected to conduct their own necessary research and study. Students will be divided into groups. Tasks including research, writing, and oral practices will be assigned both to individual students and groups.

costype: 領域課程-公民與倫理思考
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
我國民法繼受德國民法典，而有民法總則的設置。民法總則編沿襲19世紀學說匯纂（Pandektenwissenschaft）學者的理念，認為權利主體、權利客體及法律行為是私法的基本構成元素，故應在所有民法篇章之前加以規定。這個理念，使民法總則的規範內容過於抽象、脫離生活現實。故本課程設計上將以具體之契約類型（如買賣）為基礎，結合具體案例，使學生較容易掌握民法總則中各項法律概念的內容。為此，本課程內容之範圍將不限於民法總則的條文，依課程需要，亦將跨及債編總論、債編各論、物權甚至身份法之領域，俾使學生能在學習民法的初步階段能對民事法有。本課程雖名之為民法總則，然實際內容上則較接近於民事財產法導論，此亦符合目前德國大學法學院之主流趨勢。此外，為使大一新生能儘速適應法律系考試的答題方式，本課程特別安排實例演習時間，使學生在面對多變之案例事實時，也能熟練運用法條。儘管如此，本課程仍保留合理限度之學術性質，為學生在往後的法律學習打造堅實的基礎。
主要課程內容：
法律適用的基本概念、民事法的規範體系、權利主體論、法律行為論、權利客體論、代理制度、消滅時效、條件、期限與消滅時效
學習目標：
1. 建立對私法關係的基礎認識
2. 法律解釋、抽象法律概念及民法學說理論之掌握。
3. 借重請求權基礎思維，學習將法律適用於具體個案之方法。
預期學習成果：
初步學習到民法規範私人間關係之基礎規範架構，認識個別規範間之關連，瞭解解釋法律之不同方式（法學方法論），以請求權基礎之思考方式，分析具體個案事實，以奠定未來學習債法及物權法之基礎。

上課方式：實體上課，但開放陽明校區同學以遠距方式修讀。

costype: 領域課程-公民與倫理思考
crs_outline:
法律是人類社會中重要的一環，影響生活中的各個面向。法律除了包含抽象的條文與理論，也涉及具體的社會實況。世界各國由於文化、政治、經濟等差異，形成並擁有不同的法律內涵；這些獨特的歷史經驗，影響了當代社會中的法律議題與因應之道。我們身處在台灣，應了解台灣在特有的環境與條件下，法律在過去發展及轉變的過程，連結現今法律的歷史脈絡。

本課程以台灣為主體，介紹這塊地域從以前到現在的法律秩序與內涵，包括原住民法等複數法律文明時期（史前至1683年）、以漢人法律傳統為主的清朝統治時期（1683–1895）、開始引進近代西方法的日本統治時期（1895–1945）、到中華民國時期與當代社會（1945迄今），讓學生了解曲折複雜而多元豐富的台灣法律史。

本課程將依照時序，分別探討重要的法律主題，包括憲法（政府組織與人權發展）、行政法（地方制度與選舉）、司法審判、法律專業社群（法官、檢察官、律師）、刑事法律與政策、民事法與土地關係、原住民法與權利等制度，以及這些法規在社會生活中的實際運作情形。

課程目標在於讓歷史思維進入法學研究與論證，了解外來法制與在地經驗的互動與變化過程。藉由寬廣且深遠的法律史觀，提升批判性思考的能力，建立包容與尊重差異的觀點。

memo: 限科法所碩、專、博同學選修
crs_outline:
課程為必修，修課同學必須就自己之獨立研究主題或碩士論文，以符合學術一般規範之方式，公開進行報告發表。修課同學與老師會針對報告內容予以評論、提問。目標為透過論文寫作之觀摩，練習論文之寫作與發表，提升對於議題的分析與掌握，培養對於學術報告之審閱與批評之能力。
主要課程內容:主要包含兩大部分
第一為對自己研究的進行，以及磨練口頭報告之技巧。第二部分則對於同學之報告提出回應與批評，以熟悉該領域之專業知識，並發展對議題之思考與評論之技巧。修課同學應認真聆聽報告並提出意見。除自己之報告主題外，會視修課情況，指定同學輪流擔任每與談人。與談人負有對當週報告主題提出評論之義務。
學習目標:
一、培養校級基本素養與核心能力：
＊資訊素養 
＊品德教育 
＊國際視野 
＊發現及解決問題的能力 
＊跨界多元思考的能力 
＊群己平衡的認知 
二、培養管理學院學生基本素養與核心能力：
＊發掘、分析管理相關領域問題、尋求解決答案並進行決策的能力 
三、培養科法碩學生基本素養與核心能力：
＊建立從事法律實務工作應具備的法學專業素養、國際觀與倫理思維 
＊培養對社會時事發展的觀察與分析能力 
＊發現及解決問題的能力 
＊科際間知識的整合以及實證研究方法　
預期學習成果:
若上述學習目標能力皆能具備當然最好，但在完成本課程後，學生最應該具備發表學術研究之能力、在學術會議發表之能力以及對學術作品進行思考與批判之能力。

本課程為必修，經由指導教授對碩士班研究生一對一的個別指導，以提升修課同學撰寫論文之能力，並充實修課同學之論文內容，而使修課學生在論文研究上獲得較具體的成效。

一、	針對特定議題進行研究之能力。
二、	於會議上發表論文之能力。
三、	針對特定議題進行批判、思考與對話之能力。
四、	撰寫學術文章之能力。
預期學習成果：
修習完成本課程後，學生應該具備針對特定議題進行研究之能力、於會議上發表論文之能力、針對特定議題進行批判、思考與對話之能力以及撰寫學術文章之能力。

crs_outline: With the achievements of nanotechnology and nanoscience, a wide variety of nanoscale materials and devices with different sizes (1–100 nm), shapes, and compositions have been introduced to biosensing. The small sizes of nanoparticles and nanodevices break through the limitation of structure miniaturization, leading to a lower detection limit, even reaching zeptomolar concentrations. Based on fundamentals of theories, aside from optical biosensing, this course introduces and emphysizes novel principles and detection strategies in biosensing for nanomaterials and nanodevices. crs_outline:
This course is designed to provide an in-depth introduction to Information Security Practice and Regulation. Its primary objective is to impart a comprehensive understanding of international standards of information security and the best practice for industry. Topics range from security or privacy-oriented standards such as ISO 27001/27002 (ISMS), 27701 (PIMS), 27014 (IS Governance) and 29134 (PIA) to standards for specific domains such as IEC 62443 (OT), ISO 28001 (SCM), 42001 (AIMS), 38505 (Data Governance), 23576 & 23244 (Blockchain and distributed ledger technologies).

This course offers an extensive introduction to the practices and regulations of information security, designed to equip students with a thorough understanding of the international standards governing information security and industry best practices. Our primary goal is to ensure learners acquire a deep and comprehensive knowledge of how to maintain security and privacy in various organizational contexts, guided by globally recognized standards. Throughout the course, we will cover a broad spectrum of security and privacy-oriented standards, including:

-	ISO 27001/27002 for Information Security Management Systems (ISMS),
-	ISO 27701 for Privacy Information Management Systems (PIMS),
-	ISO 27014 for Information Security Governance,
-	ISO 29134 for Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA),
-	Other domain-specific standards such as IEC 62443 (OT), ISO 28001 (SCM), ISO 42001 (AIMS), ISO 38505 (Data Governance), and ISO 23576 & 23244 (Blockchain and distributed ledger technologies).

This curriculum is carefully crafted to not only present theoretical knowledge but also to provide practical insights of these standards, preparing students for the real-world challenges they will face in the information security field.

memo: [English Medium Course]
crs_outline:
Visual computing transitioned from traditional image processing that relied on manual feature engineering to representation learning driven by deep neural networks. This transition has allowed machines to achieve unprecedented accuracy in visual recognition tasks, while simultaneously introducing challenges regarding computational efficiency, model interpretability, and multimodal reasoning. This course bridges foundational deep learning algorithms with forward-looking real-world deployments such as autonomous systems and digital healthcare.
The primary objective of this course is understanding deep learning across diverse core vision tasks, including image classification, semantic segmentation, image retrieval, and generative synthesis. We will explore limitations such as the heavy reliance on massive annotated datasets, bias amplification, and the inherent "black box" opacity of neural network architectures. Furthermore, introducing the frontier of AI, covering the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs). The synthesis of visual and textual modalities enables systems to transition from mere pattern recognition to complex compositional reasoning, spatial logic, and agentic interactions. To ensure practical viability, the course examines edge computing optimization such as model pruning for deploying highly parameterized models onto resource-constrained hardware.

memo: 視訊同步遠距課程 。醫電所(原生醫所).電機.生科. MD-PhD學程及AI學院。(通識課程) 、開放隨班附讀。
costype: 領域課程-社會中的科技與自然
crs_outline:
「大自然用了38億年完成研發，我們的任務不是重新發明輪子，而是學會向大自然學習」～～
''Nature has spent 3.8 billion years perfecting its designs. Our job is not to reinvent the wheel, but to learn from nature.''   ~ George

本課程為國內首創以「仿生科技（Biomimcry）」為名之課程，旨在引導學生從自然界與生命科學中汲取靈感，探索生物如何透過數十億年的演化，發展出高效率、高適應性且極具智慧的結構、機制與功能，進而應用於工程設計、醫療照護、智慧科技及產業創新之中。

仿生科技的核心精神在於「向自然學習」。無論是壁虎的附著能力啟發新型黏著材料、蓮葉效應發展自潔表面、蝙蝠與海豚的回聲定位技術促成感測系統創新，或人體組織與器官功能啟發新世代醫療器材設計，皆展現了仿生科技跨越生物與工程領域的巨大潛力。

本課程將聚焦於「生醫 × 仿生 × 創新設計」跨領域整合，結合生物學、基礎醫學、生物科技、資訊通訊技術（ICT）及工程設計等知識，引導學生觀察自然現象、分析真實需求、建立仿生思維，並將其轉化為具創新價值的解決方案。

課程採開放式與問題導向學習（Problem-Based Learning, PBL）模式進行，透過案例討論、團隊合作、主題探究及成果實作等方式，培養學生從生活中的不便、未被滿足的需求、社會問題或疾病挑戰出發，學習如何從自然界尋找靈感與解決策略。學生除需發展創新構想外，亦將學習需求分析、利害關係人分析、設計思考、科技創新及成果溝通等重要能力。

為強化創新創業與產業接軌能力，本課程亦導入創投提案（Pitching）概念，將傳統成果發表轉化為模擬創業募資發表會，培養學生以故事化方式呈現創新價值，並鼓勵優秀團隊與產業界、研發單位或競賽平台進行交流，提升創新成果之實踐機會。

修習本課程後，學生將能：
1. 了解仿生科技之基本概念、發展歷程及應用領域。
2. 建立觀察自然現象與生物特徵之能力，培養跨域學習視野。
3. 學習從生物結構、功能與行為中萃取可轉譯之工程設計原理。
4. 培養需求分析、問題定義與創新構想發展能力。
5. 建立團隊合作、跨領域溝通及設計思考能力。
6. 學習以創投簡報及故事敘述方式展現創新成果價值。
7. 具備將仿生概念應用於生醫工程、智慧醫療及未來科技發展之能力。

本課程不只是學習生物如何運作，更重要的是學習如何從自然界尋找答案，並將其轉化為改變世界的創新科技。因此藉由『仿生科技』這門課融合智慧醫電所推動方向（智慧醫療、臨床需求導向、仿生設計、創新創業），讓我們一起把課程定位成：從觀察生命到創造科技（From Life Observation to Technology Innovation）。

crs_outline:
Bio-lab on a chip (Bio-LOC) is a device that integrates several laboratory functions on a single chip; It deals with the handling of extremely small fluid volumes. Bio-LOC is closely related to, and overlaps with, microfluidics, which describes primarily the physics, the manipulation and study of minute amounts of fluids. The devices are a subset of MEMS devices and often indicated by "Micro Total Analysis Systems" (μTAS) as well. Several specific topics will be taught in this course that includes: 1. Microfluidic devices, 2. DNA microarrays, 3. Protein microarrays, 4. Nano-biosensor, 5. Single DAN sequence, and et al. The field of this course covers basic chemistry, biochemistry, nano-technology, semi-conductance-technology, and applications of these multidisciplinary sciences. 

醫療科技的發展，個人化醫學的需求逐漸浮現。微小化、智慧化、高通量化與遠距化成為是技術的生醫發展的共同趨勢。本課程主旨在使同學對生物晶片有基本之認識，內容將涵蓋microfluidic devices, DNA microarrays，protein microarrays之操作原理，製作過程，以及應用範圍。課程中將生物晶片之種類與適用問題進行科學性、通俗性與系統性介紹，讓學生能夠有系統學習、易懂、並能實用。同時希望學生能藉由瞭解生物晶片及各式生醫系統之原理，引領學生對生物醫學檢測等基礎知識有所認知。並能啟發學生將來能協助生醫微製造技術(BioMEMS)的發展。因此課程設計上包括：1. 課程講授。2.學期末報告。另外上課以英文簡報介紹，培養學生未來以英文吸收專業知識之能力。

cos_cname: 研究對象權益之保障與法律議題
memo: 醫電所(原生醫所)主開(通識課程)
cos_ename: Protection of Research Subjects Rights and Legal Issues
costype: 領域課程-公民與倫理思考
crs_outline:
一、課程目標
（一）瞭解以「人」為研究對象之倫理與法規。
（二）探討研究對象權益保護之實務案例。
（三）學習研究計畫審查內容及參與者同意書之撰寫。
The goal is to: (a) understand the research ethics and regulations of  human subject research,(b) explore the case of protection of research subjects rights, and(c) learn to write research protocols and consents of research subjects.
二、課程概述
保護以「人」為研究對象之權益，已成為研究者應遵守的普世價值。我國於2011年12月28日公布施行之《人體研究法》，即是落實人體研究有關研究對象之保護，並且要求研究者進行研究前，應擬定研究計畫，經倫理審查委員會審查通過，始可為之。再者，以「人」為研究對象之相關法規，尚有《醫療法》、《人體試驗管理辦法》、《藥品優良臨床試驗作業準則》、《醫療器材管理法》、《醫療器材優良臨床試驗管理辦法》、《人體生物資料庫管理條例》、《個人資料保護法》等，故研究者進行研究時，亦應注意上述法規有關研究對象保護之特別規定，以免觸犯法令規定。是以，本課程首先是要讓學生了解研究倫理概念與相關規範，包括研究倫理之源起、原則與法令，以重視研究倫理之重要性。其次，透過實務案例之討論與分析，讓學生認識有關研究對象權益保護之法規內容，避免違反法令規定。最後，協助學生撰寫研究計畫書與參與者同意書，以申請倫理審查委員會之審查。
本課程設計包括：（一）以「人」為研究對象之研究倫理與相關法規的講授。（二）個人書面報告及討論。（三）撰寫研究計畫書與參與者同意書。希冀同學進行有關「人」的研究行為符合研究倫理與相關法規之規定，並且有撰寫研究計畫書與參與者同意書之能力，以獲得倫理審查委員會之審查通過，讓研究行為具有正當性及合法性。
The protection of research subjects rights has become a universal value that researchers should observe. The “ Human Subjects Research Act"  took effect on December 28, 2011. This Act is specially stipulated to regulate the right protection of human research subjects. Prior to conduct a research, the principal investigator shall submit the research protocol for review and approval by the Institutional Review Board (hereinafter “IRB"). Furthermore, the relevant laws and regulations on protection of research subjects rights include the “ Medical Care Act", “ Regulations on Human Trials ", “ Regulations for Good Clinical Practice", “ Medical Devices Act",“ Regulations on Good Clinical Practice for Medical Devices" ,“ Human Biobank Management Act", and “ Personal Data Protection Act". Therefore, before conducting research, you should also pay attention to the special provisions of the above-mentioned laws and regulations on protection of research subjects to avoid violating laws and regulations. This course is to enable students to understand the concept and related norms of research ethics, including the origin, principles and regulations. Secondly, through the discussion and analysis of cases, students can understand the contents of regulations related to protection of research subjects rights. Finally, students can learn to write research protocols and consents of research subjects to apply for review by IRB.

memo: 醫電所(原生醫所).生科.MD-PhD學程.應化、開放隨班附讀
crs_outline:
化學是理解生命現象、疾病機制、藥物作用及生物醫學工程技術的重要基礎。然而，許多工程與資訊背景的學生往往對化學感到陌生甚至畏懼，使得在學習生醫相關知識時遭遇不小的門檻。

事實上，化學與我們的日常生活及健康照護息息相關。例如：COVID-19期間常見的酒精乾洗手成分為何？次氯酸水與漂白水有何差異？是否可以直接接觸皮膚？疫苗是如何研發出來的？症狀治療藥物與抗病毒藥物有何不同？藥用洗髮精與一般洗髮精的成分差異在哪裡？食品添加物、塑化劑、三聚氰胺、銅葉綠素等議題又隱含哪些化學原理？此外，藥品仿單上那些看似艱深的英文化學名稱，究竟代表什麼意義？

本課程將以生物醫學工程的觀點出發，結合生活案例、醫療應用及時事議題，介紹化學在人體、生物材料、藥物、醫療器材及健康照護中的角色。課程內容兼顧基礎理論與實務應用，透過深入淺出的方式，協助學生建立生醫化學的核心概念，培養判讀醫療與健康資訊的能力，並為未來進階生醫工程、智慧醫療、生物科技及臨床應用相關課程奠定基礎。

修習本課程後，學生將能：
1. 建立生醫化學之基本知識與核心概念。
2. 了解化學原理在人體、生理、疾病及醫療中的應用。
3. 具備閱讀與理解常見藥物、保健食品及醫療產品成分資訊的能力。
4. 能以科學觀點分析生活中的健康與醫療相關議題。
5. 建立跨領域思維，銜接生物醫學工程、智慧醫療及生技產業之進階學習需求。

如果您覺得化學很可怕，那麼這門課正是為您而設計；如果您覺得化學很有趣，那麼這門課將帶您看見化學如何改變醫療、科技與人類健康。

crs_outline:
This course focuses on the fundamentals of medical image processing and its applications in machine learning. Students will systematically learn essential techniques such as image sampling and quantization, image enhancement, edge detection and sharpening, spatial domain filtering, morphological operations, image analysis, and segmentation. Special emphasis will be placed on feature extraction—a critical step for tasks like image segmentation and classification using machine learning. Through hands-on Python programming, students will bridge theory and practice to solve real-world problems in medical imaging. This course also serves as a foundational step toward deep learning in the following semester.
*Course Objectives
1. Master fundamental image processing techniques: Understand and implement basic algorithms for sampling, quantization, enhancement, and filtering.
2. Develop strong feature extraction skills: Learn to extract discriminative statistical, morphological, and texture features from images for machine learning models.
3. Apply machine learning to medical images: Use classification and segmentation models to address real-world challenges in medical imaging and evaluate model performance.
4. Strengthen Python programming skills: Build complete image processing and machine learning pipelines using Python and key libraries (e.g., NumPy, OpenCV, scikit-image, scikit-learn).
5. Foster problem-solving mindset: Gain the ability to analyze new imaging problems, select appropriate techniques, and rapidly prototype solutions, laying a solid foundation for future work in deep learning.

crs_outline:
The goal to attend the colloquium is to expand the knowledge of science. But the goal to write the report is to practice on documenting the info with the consciousness of training yourself on publishing/sharing what you found through listening to the lecture in a way as if you are writing an article of your own work with the exception that the data and finding are from the speaker. This way you internalize the knowledge and logical framework.

Importantly, do not practice plagiarism by directly copy and paste any wording or Figures of speakers or any other source. The wording has to be rephrased while the Figure can be copied only if the source is clearly and copy right are clearly specified. 

Two-three pages concise report for each lecture that contains the following points.

Points 1-4 are basics and Point 5 is additional.

1.	Short introduction of the speaker with the affiliation specified.
2.	The big picture or the background of the scientific problem (better with graphic to illuminate).
3.	The niche or novel approach the speaker tackles the problem (better with graphic to illuminate).
4.	The major findings (better with graphic, you can practice to create a Graphic Abstract to summarize).
5.	Potential impact of the work. 
6.	Student comments: what you have been inspired? or you want to place critics on the speaker’s science and/or presentation.

Syllabus 1
1.	Surface and Interface
– surface energy, surface reconstruction, domain boundary, crystal shapes
2.	Diffusion and Mass Transport
– atomistic picture, surface/interface diffusion, diffusion in solids (battery) and soft matters
3.	Nucleation and Growth
– homogeneous/heterogeneous nucleation, thin film growth modes, growth of nanocrystals and 2D materials.
4.	Self-Assembly
– driving force of self-assembly, quantum dots, nanostructures
5.	Adsorption
– porous materials, ultracapacitors, MOFs, catalysis
6.	Mechanical Properties
– mechanical properties of nanocrystalline materials, CNTs, 2D materials, device stability
7.	Microstructure of Multicomponent Materials
– entropic mixing, phase segregation, chemically complex materials
References: relevant literatures in each subjects

crs_outline:
Advanced Metrology, Spectroscopy and Microscopy: Fundamentals and Applications 
COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING
Taiwan International Graduate Program for Sustainable Chemical Science  
Instructor LI-CHYONG CHEN 

This course offers a comprehensive exploration of physical measurements, starting with the foundational concepts of time, space, and mass. These fundamentals serve as a stepping stone to more specialized studies, including the technology and methods surrounding vacuum measurement. The curriculum then transitions into a detailed examination of electron dynamics and properties, an area that spans several key technologies.

The discussion on electron dynamics begins with electrochemistry, where students will delve into how electron measurements influence material science through chemical processes. This segment seamlessly leads into the study of magnetism and spintronics, where participants will learn about magnetic properties and spin dynamics, exploring various measurement techniques such as Hall effects and Josephson junctions. The course further extends into electron microscopy, specifically through Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) and Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM), which are pivotal in characterizing materials at the atomic level.

As we explore these dynamic properties, we also focus on thermal measurements—a critical yet often underdeveloped area in physics. This part of the course covers thermal physics, including calorimetry, temperature measurements, and thermal transport measurements. Topics range from classical diffusive and ballistic transport to advanced quantum and anomalous transport phenomena. This section is vital for understanding the energy aspects of physical properties and their measurement challenges.

Following the deep dive into electron-related technologies and thermal phenomena, the course shifts focus to the study of light and photonics. This section covers a range of photon-based techniques, including X-ray and neutron diffraction, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and surface spectroscopies like X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) and Ultraviolet Photoelectron Spectroscopy (UPS). Additionally, photoluminescence spectroscopy is discussed, highlighting its application in studying material properties. The course concludes with advanced optical imaging techniques such as Scanning Near-field Optical Microscopy (SNOM) and ultrafast pump-probe transient absorption spectroscopy, which are essential for understanding interactions within nanostructured materials.

Through a structured progression from basic principles to complex technologies, the course equips students with a thorough understanding of measurement techniques and their application across diverse scientific fields. This approach not only underscores the interconnectedness of these techniques but also their crucial roles in advancing contemporary scientific research and technological innovation.

課程目標(中文) ：
1. 運用分子軌域理論、對稱性及配位場理論，描述過渡金屬錯合物的電子結構。
2. 解讀紫外-可見光、紅外線及電子順磁共振光譜數據，推導金屬錯合物的結構與鍵結。
3. 解釋有機金屬鍵結概念（18電子規則、配位數及π反鍵），並應用於常見配位基系統。
4. 分析配位基取代、電子轉移及基本有機金屬反應步驟的機制。
5. 描述並評估過渡金屬催化循環，包括交叉偶聯、氫化反應及C–H活化。
6. 連結生物無機化學原理與金屬蛋白及金屬酵素的功能。
7. 討論無機材料、奈米結構的最新進展及當代研究文獻。
8. 以英語清晰表達無機化學概念，並完成正式口頭報告。
*課程目標(英文) ：
1. Apply molecular orbital theory, symmetry, and ligand field theory to describe the electronic structure of transition-metal complexes.
2. Interpret UV-Vis, IR, and EPR spectroscopic data to deduce the structure and bonding of metal complexes.
3. Explain organometallic bonding concepts (18-electron rule, hapticity, and π-backbonding) and apply them to common ligand systems.
4. Analyze the mechanisms of ligand substitution, electron transfer, and fundamental organometallic reaction steps.
5. Describe and evaluate transition-metal catalytic cycles, including cross-coupling, hydrogenation, and C–H activation.
6. Relate principles of bioinorganic chemistry to the function of metalloproteins and metalloenzymes.
7. Discuss recent advances in inorganic materials, nanostructures, and the current research literature.
8. Communicate inorganic chemistry concepts clearly in English, including through a formal oral presentation.

cos_ename: Special Topics on Legal Research Methodology
crs_outline:
一直以來我國法律學研究受到法律繼受文化與註釋法學的桎梏，往往造成法學解釋與實務應用上的落差。法律研究方法之中，法學實證研究屬於其中重要內容。法學實證研究將透過資訊的分析、比對，正可用於檢驗法律適用之可行性或不足之處。擬以法學實證研究作為論文研究方法、或對此研究方法有興趣之同學， 歡迎選修此門課程。

傳統法學研究，著重外國法制的比較介紹，以及法律自主體系的邏輯，無法真正反應法律現象。而法律之實際運作狀況，法律對於社會產生之影響，以及法律與其他社會科學的互動關係，都有待實際資料的蒐集與驗證，而非先驗學說理論可以解答。本課程之目標，係以介紹重要法學研究方法，其中以法學實證研究（empirical legal study）為其中重點，包括其意涵及其研究方法為主，透過實際案例、學者論述的分析研讀以及實際操作，引導同學思考法學實證研究的時代意義。

主要課程內容：
1.	學習實證分析之基本概念
2.	了解基礎統計概念
3.	瞭解相關之統計軟體與資料庫

學習目標：
期許學生能透過掌握法學實證研究方法，並以此作為論文研究工具之一。

預期學習成果：
1.	對於實證方法有相當的瞭解，並能指出傳統法學理論之問題
2.	對統計與實證方法有相當之瞭解，並瞭解其優點與限制具備進行實證研究與使用統計軟體之基礎能力

crs_outline: 《犯罪網絡與大數據分析》是一門結合理論、工具實作與犯罪情境應用的進階課程，旨在帶領學生以「網絡」觀點理解犯罪行為與犯罪組織的互動結構，並進一步延伸至複雜網絡分析與大型網絡資料的處理策略。課程聚焦社會網絡分析在犯罪領域的研究與實務案例，使用 NodeXL、UCINET、Gephi 與 Python 等工具完成網絡繪圖、結構特徵判讀、社群偵測與關鍵節點辨識。同時，課程將導入 AI 工具協助資料清理、實體解析與關係建立，此外讓學生學習監督式學習、非監督式學習與強化學習等方法，並實作整合 SNA 與大數據分析進行犯罪風險預測、群體分群與偵查線索發掘，培養從資料到洞見、從洞見到決策建議的完整能力。

crs_outline:
課程概述】：
1提供燃燒理論 及熱釋放率的火源設計等基本火災動力學概念
2.提供建築物火災的火燄高度,火羽流, 延燒, 天花板噴射流 及 輻射效應 以及煙層高度及厚度, 通風流, 煙囪效應, 中性帶運算等基本理論課程。
3.提供各種防火感熱元件以及運用火焰波長及跳動頻率,及各種火警煙濃度元件探測原理探討以及能見度影響評估。
4.提供建築防火工程有關燃燒基礎概論、設計工學手法、防火材料及消防設備運用及建築規劃設計等課程。
5.提供煙控與避難安全設計、建築區劃與構造防火設計、建築重大火災案例分析等理論及實務。
6.提供火災爆炸基本原理、預防技術、爆炸防護工程及案例分析等防火防爆理論與實務。 
【課程目標】：
本學科將讓學生1.了解火災及爆炸之基本知識。2.學習建築火災及爆炸預防與控制工程技術。3. 配合專題課程及重大火災及爆炸案例分析，將理論與實務結合。4.提供職場上能正確、有效應用的防火與防爆技術。

cos_ename: Organic Semiconducting and Electro-Optical Materials and Devices
dep_cname: 工學院碩士在職專班-半導體組
dep_ename: Degree Program of Semiconductor Material and Processing Equipment
crs_outline:
簡介有機半導體(含介電材料)、有機光電(含光學及非線性光學材料)、AI矽光子(含光纖及光調變器材料)、及軟性電子(含高分子封裝複合材料)等材料及其元件之原理與分析
Introduction to organic semiconductors (including dielectric materials), organic optoelectronics (including optical and nonlinear optical materials), AI silicon photonics (including optical fiber and optical modulator materials), and flexible electronics (including polymer packaging composite materials) and the principles and analysis of their components.

A. 軟性電子及有機半導體材料簡介 (Introduction to Flexible Electronic, Organic Semiconducting, and Dielectric Materials) 
1. 高分子材料簡介 (Introduction to Polymers) 
2. 軟性電子及有機半導體與介電材料 (Flexible Electronic, Organic Semiconducting, and Dielectric Materials) 
3. 有機薄膜電晶體材料及元件 (Organic Thin Film Transistor Materials) 
B. 有機光電及高分子材料簡介 (Introduction to Electro-Optical Polymer Materials) 
1. 液晶及液晶高分子材料 (Liquid Crystal and Liquid Crystal Polymer Materials) 
2. 有機及高分子發光二極體材料 (OLED and PLED Materials) 
3. 有機及高分子太陽能電池材料 (Organic and Polymeric Solar Cell Materials) 
4. 有機及高分子非線性光學材料 (Organic and Polymeric Nonlinear Optical Materials) 
5. 矽光子AI及共封裝光學材料 (AI Silicon Photonics and Co-Packaged Optical Materials) 
C. 材料性質介紹 (Introduction to Properties of Materials) 
1. 材料電學性質 (Electrical Properties of Materials) 
2. 材料熱學性質 (Thermal Properties of Materials) 
3. 材料光學性質 (Optical Properties of Materials) 
D. 有機發光二極體顯示材料及元件 (OLED and PLED Display Materials and Devices) 
1. 有機發光二極體材料基本介紹 (Introduction to OLED and PLED Materials) 
	1.1. 化學結構 (Chemical Structures) 
	1.2. 物理性質 (Physical Properties) 
2. 有機發光二極體之應用物性與量測 (Physical Properties and Measurements of OLEDs) 
3. 有機發光二極體相關原理及元件 (Principle and Devices of OLEDs and PLEDs) 
4. 有機發光二極體相關材料及製程 (Device Materials and Process of OLEDs and PLEDs) 
	4.1. 有機發光二極體製程 (Process of OLEDs and PLEDs) 
	4.2. 電極基板 (Electrode and Substrate of OLEDs and PLEDs) 
	4.3. 發光層 (Light-Emitting Layer) 
	4.4. 電子傳輸層 (Electron Transporting Layer) 
	4.5. 電洞傳輸層 (Hole Transporting Layer)
E. 液晶顯示材料及元件 (LC Display Materials and Devices) 
1. 液晶材料基本介紹 (Introduction to LCs) 
1.1液晶分類 (Classification of LCs) 
1.2 化學結構 (Chemical Structures) 
1.3 物理性質 (Physical Properties) 
2. 液晶之應用物性與量測 (Electro-Optical Properties of LCs) 
3. 液晶顯示相關原理及元件 (Principle and Devices of LCDs) 
4. 液晶顯示相關元件材料及製程 (Device Materials and Process of LCDs) 
4.1. 液晶顯示器製程 (Process of LCDs) 
4.2. 液晶顯示相關元件材料：透明基板 (Substrate)、透明電極 (ITO)、配向層 (Alignment Layer)、間隙物 (Spacer)、彩色濾光片 (Color Filter)、偏光板 (Polarizer)、補償膜 (Compensation Film)、及光源及導光配件 (Backlighting System)

crs_outline:
光電科學與實驗技術 Electro-optical Science and Experimental Technology
1. 從人類對於光的研究視角來看科學發展，並適時帶入基礎物理觀念與前瞻物理應用。學習光的波動性、光電材料、元件和系統設計。 Introduce scientific development from the perspective of human research on light, and introduce basic physical concepts and prospective physical applications in a timely manner. Stusy Electro-optical Science and Experimental Technology, including fundamental topics in wave nature of light, optoelectronic materials, devices, and system design. 
2. 藉由實驗實作，了解光學各種基本現象與應用。一方面得以加深以往課本知識的理解程度，另一方面亦可習得基本光學實驗技術、儀器原理、光電科技之應用、與分析能力，奠定未來從事研究的基礎、啟發光學與光電系統實作能力。 Students will understand various basic phenomena and applications of optics through experimental implementation. On the one hand, students can deepen their understanding of previous textbook knowledge. On the other hand, they can also acquire basic optical experimental techniques, instrument principles, optoelectronic technology, and analysis capabilities, laying the foundation for future research and inspiring the ability to implement optical and optoelectronic systems.  
3. 實驗設備：幾何光學與像差實驗；光纖技術與特性實驗；干涉儀實驗系統~邁克遜、牛頓環、法布里-培洛等干涉儀；光的繞射、富氏光學、與光信號處理；偏極化實驗系統；固態雷射與倍頻實驗系統(含Q開關脈衝雷射與時域量測)；雷射鑷夾；電光調制實驗(圓錐光干涉)；醫療雷射光電應用系統；Schlieren實驗系統(氣流紋影)；空間光相位調製器(LCoS數位光學系統)；近紅外光譜系統

crs_outline:
This course is designed to introduce students to the field of Machine Learning, starting from Python programming fundamentals to mastering core data science techniques. It covers essential topics including data preprocessing, feature engineering, and mainstream machine learning algorithms (such as regression, classification, clustering, and dimensionality reduction).
In addition to mastering practical tools like Scikit-learn, students will be introduced to multilayer neural networks and the PyTorch deep learning framework. By balancing theory with hands-on practice, students will develop the skills to process data, build models, and perform evaluations from scratch. The course concludes with a final project where students apply their knowledge to solve real-world data problems.
本課程旨在帶領學生進入機器學習的世界，從 Python 程式基礎出發，逐步深入資料科學的核心技術。課程涵蓋資料前處理、特徵工程、以及主流的機器學習演算法（包含回歸、分類、分群與降維）。除了掌握 Scikit-learn 等實務工具，學生也將接觸多層神經網路與 PyTorch 深度學習框架。透過理論與實作並重的教學方式，學生將具備從零開始處理數據、建構模型並進行評估的能力，最終能獨立完成具備實務意義的期末專案，解決現實世界中的數據問題。

crs_outline: Strategic management is concerned with managing the competitive position (including the general environment, industry and market structure, and organizational strengths and weaknesses) and long-term development of the business enterprise. This course aims to relate the principles and issues addressed in the various functional business areas to introduce an integrated concept of management and provide an understanding of the relationship between theory and practice in general management. The course will lead students into two main areas which must be analyzed in order to formulate and implement a well-conceived strategy: the external environment of the firm (the industry context), and the internal environment of the firm (its resources and capabilities). Some of the key topics covered include: (1) exploring why and how good strategic management increases business performance, (2) the application of a set of analytical frameworks, (3) analyzing the reasons for the success and failure of a firm, and (4) the methods of developing an effective competitive strategy and executing it competently. The teaching materials include lectures, case analyses, and independent readings.

1.介紹個體經濟的供需理論、需求彈性、賽局理論、效用與消費者選擇、貨幣時間價值和機會成本的經濟觀念，幫助學生運用經濟分析理解企業決策與個人行為，教學過程中加入台灣經濟社會的實際例子,以彰顯理論之實用性。
2.闡述總體經濟的財政政策、貨幣政策與安倍經濟學，幫助學生理解政府施政目的與經濟結果。講解國際經濟學熱錢對外匯市場、金融資產和房地產的影響，讓學生理解金融風暴成因後果。
3.介紹經濟學理論，加入台灣企業或新聞的實際例子,加深課程的實用性，課堂中使用經濟學家提出的圖形與簡單的數學,配合文字說明，培養學生經濟直覺與興趣。訓練學生經濟分析的數學技巧，用簡單的微分計算加強學生經濟概念的了解。
4.培養學生欣賞經濟學家在經濟專門期刊上的論文,並能質疑報章雜誌上報導爭議，有系統的、全面性的、循序漸進引導學生發現經濟議題，進而撰寫學位論文畢業。
5. 經濟學是證券投資顧問事業證券投資分析人員、高普考金融保險組、公股銀行的招募考試相關科目，本課程教導就業考試較常出題的題型，幫助學生就業與考取證照。

課程概述與目標：
1.Students are required to read the articles indicated in the reading lists. The lecture will be given according to the articles.

2.Students are required to give a presentation on their chosen topic. The materials are the case studies related to the weekly topic so that they can apply the conceptual framework on the real cases. Presentations can be given less for a maximum of 20 minutes and a joint discussion followed after it. Presentations are to be prepared in PowerPoint, and should ensure that the necessary time limits. A hard copy of the slides should be given to the course coordinator prior to the oral presentation.

3.Students are required to complete one case report by the end of the semester. The title for the paper will be given during the course. The paper should demonstrate an understanding of the issues raised in the relevant lecture, and brings personal critical or creative viewpoints for the particular topic.

crs_outline:
課程概述：
本課程將會介紹目前在數位內容系統設計的原理與技術。上課的同學將在此豐富內涵的領域中得到非常實用的經驗和技術。課程的主題包含了數位內容資訊的形成和管理、多媒體的有效呈現與處理方式，以及圖形、音效和音樂、影像和視訊等資料的製作，配合多媒體的軟硬體系統，完成實作和整合；同時介紹人工智慧與機器學習在圖形識別、智慧醫療等的應用，探討電子商務實務上數位內容所扮演的關鍵角色。

課程目標：
本課程針對數位內容理論與應用，對數位內容系統和標準,在資訊、教育、娛樂和商務上的應用，給予一個概括全面性的介紹。近來由於人工智慧與機器學習透過硬體計算能力的提昇，可以自動擷取資料的特徵，將運用Matlab語言的深度學習套件和函數，探討相關深度學習的模型，優化參數及避免過度配適，以提高模型應用的準確度。實作案例涵蓋時間序列分析、圖像辨識、以及自然語言處理應用在網際網路的市場行銷和電子商務。

crs_outline: Algorithmic game theory and learning sprouts as an active interdisciplinary field integrating computer science and economics. While its impacting contributions, namely, the efficiency of equilibria and complexity of computing equilibria are more on the measurement and analysis side of equilibria, treating equilibria as an engineerable aggregated choice, “algorithmic mechanism design and social choice” which is more on the engineering side also develops promisingly in parallel and produces lots of interesting and well-unknown results. Based on the classical results in mechanism design and social choice in economics, our goals are introducing various mechanism design questions and topics from computational and algorithmic perspectives, complementary to  algorithmic game theory and learning.

crs_outline:
The "Research Methods and Thesis Writing in Technology Management" course offers a holistic learning structure, enabling students to grasp the essentials of academic research and scholarly writing. Beginning with the aims of social science research, it progresses to an in-depth exploration of literature review strategies and fundamental database familiarity. Students are equipped to gather primary and secondary data, execute quantitative and qualitative analyses, and finalize their thesis writing. The curriculum particularly highlights the development of management theories, examining theoretical perspectives across various dimensions, and the recontextualization of theoretical narratives. With a focus on the principles of thesis composition, structural organization, and textual logic, the course prepares students to undertake technology management research and author dissertations within this specialized domain.

crs_outline:
This course provides a high-level framework for integrating Statistical Learning with strategic Decision Making in the age of artificial intelligence. Unlike traditional computational courses that focus on manual algorithmic implementation, this curriculum prioritizes "Strategic Command." We focus on the transition from predictive modeling to empirical determination. By utilizing advanced computational diagnostics, we prioritize the more critical challenges of model interpretation, risk assessment, and the exercise of human judgment in high-stakes organizational environments.
2. Learning Objectives
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
•	Orchestrate Multi-Model Frameworks: Efficiently manage and evaluate various statistical learning architectures to support organizational objectives.
•	Master Decision Diagnostics: Apply Statistical Learning principles to identify hidden biases and variances in complex data outputs.
•	Execute Strategic Decision Making: Convert technical predictions into actionable outcomes, emphasizing the human "judgment call."
•	Evaluate Algorithmic Integrity: Audit the reliability of automated systems through the lens of empirical logic and practical risk management.

在人工智慧、數位轉型與全球競爭快速發展的時代，創新能力已成為企業與組織創造競爭優勢與長期價值的關鍵。在技術快速演進的背景下，人類最重要的競爭優勢之一，正是創意思考與創新能力。企業對於能夠結合創意思考、問題解決與創新管理能力的人才需求正持續增加。創意思維亦被視為未來職場最重要的核心能力之一。具備創意思維的人才能夠在高度不確定與複雜的環境中辨識新機會、提出創新解決方案，並進一步推動組織轉型與價值創造。

本課程以「創新管理與創意問題解決」為核心，系統性介紹創意、創新與價值創造的理論基礎與實務方法。本課程透過案例分析、遊戲式學習、創意工具、設計思考、AI 輔助創新工具以及團隊專題等多元教學方式，協助學生理解創新如何在組織中被激發、管理與落實。

本課程特別為科技產業與企業組織中的在職專業人士所設計，協助學生培養在複雜且快速變動的商業環境中，發現問題、產生創意、發展創新方案並推動創新專案的能力，進而提升組織創新與價值創造的能力。

完成本課程後，學生將能夠：
•	理解創意、創新與價值創造之間的關係。
•	說明創新管理的主要理論與管理架構。
•	應用創意思考工具與方法，解決實際商業與組織問題並發展創新方案。
•	在跨領域團隊中合作，提出具可行性與創新性的解決方案。

crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
本課程為競爭法基礎課程，以我國公平交易法（公平法）為主，輔以美國、歐盟及日本競爭法說明我國競爭法現有及應有之解釋與適用。公平法施行至今已有三十年歷史。期間臺灣的產業從傳統製造業、先進電子製造業等產業發展至今日的數位科技產業，因此公平法的內涵也應與時俱進，維持市場競爭及促進經濟發展。基此，本課程旨在講授傳統限制競爭行為的規範、理論與案例，並說明傳統規範在新興的的數位科技下應如何發展。

主要課程內容包括：
1. 公平法基礎介紹
2. 限制競爭（聯合行為、獨占行為及結合）
3. 不公平競爭

學習目標：
1. 瞭解公平法架構、相關經濟學理論及實務案例
2. 重要產業之產業架構及商業模式
3. 能初步找到產業的公平法問題及進行初步分析

本課程將接續上學期美國公司法，繼續就美國公司法近二十年的最新演進相關案例與教科書資料，進行講解。本課程會需要一些英文基本的閱讀能力。基本上每週大約15頁精讀。美國公司法為所有商法、金融法領域最核心關鍵之課程，相關問題之理解，將決定後續此一領域之發展可能。
本學期課程為二學分，每週上課三小時。集中十一次上完。上課形式會混合線上與實體。基本上一次實體、一次線上進行。
實際進行方式如下：第一次上課時，會由老師公布本學期閱讀教材。每位同學也可跟老師個別討論所欲研究的主題（或由老師協助尋找研究主題），共同討論可閱讀的文獻。

dep_cname: 科技法律研究所碩士在職專班
crs_outline:
本課程採共生競爭模式設計。法律組提供制度分析，理工組提供技術現實，商管組提供市場視角，行政組提供組織效率。學生在課程中累積能力與作品，主持人則透過課程形成跨域研究與政策分析平台。
本課程模仿實務，以台灣AI治理政策擬定為目標(日後希望藉此培養企業內部AI治理專業能力)，盼由全體學生完成競爭法下AI治理宣言與政策建議成果。
本課程以互利共生競爭理論（Symbiotic and Mutually Beneficial Competition）為母理論：主張在特殊領域如AI生態系，競爭來源也會來自合作，甚至競爭秩序內生於合作結構，非必然由政府外加於其上。課程透過選定AI模型與基礎層、模型協力層與應用層互動，無論係產業真實訊息或假設例子，觀察競爭是否可內化生態系，並了解AI治理若嵌入模型協議與其他設計層面之合約或其他可參考因應方式，而非由主管機關全面主導介入。
課程運用此理論脈絡，將公平交易法規範對應至AI生態系3層結構（基礎層、模型協力層、應用層），透過團隊合作方式，引導學生自實務思考AI生態系競爭秩序政策宣言，日後進入實務甚至希望該宣言可資提出，作為某AI產業向政府提出之備查文件。課程主張主管機關不僅查察處罰，應可成助我國事業走向國際制度設計者。
本課程主要係以分組協力方式，結合法律、商管、資訊工程等不同領域，每週面對面討論，最終共同完成AI政策宣言文件，學期末提交校方陳在方教授，甚至年底講師公平會學術研討會會發表若干研究發現。

課程簡介：
本課程將透過介紹憲法規範及大法官解釋、憲法法庭裁判，使修課學生理解憲法的重要理論與概念，培養學生對於憲政時事與人權議題的興趣，以及訓練法學思維與寫作的能力。

主要課程內容：
1. 導論：憲法基本原理原則、憲政發展與變遷。
2. 司法違憲審查制度。
3. 基本人權：平等權、人身自由、言論自由、非列舉基本權等。

學習目標：
1. 理解我國憲法之規定、原理原則、重要司法解釋。
2. 對於憲法問題進行體系性的思辨，並且能以精確的法律文字進行分析。

預期學習成果：
1. 對於憲法上主要概念與基本原理原則，我國憲政制度及重要之司法解釋，具備相當的理解。
2. 具備以憲法觀點分析議題的能力，並且能夠檢索、引用相關法學文獻，並以專業的法學寫作方式書寫。
3. 關心我國憲政實況與人權議題。

上課方式：教師講授、課堂討論、及實例演習。

請修課學生特別留意，上課時間為18:45-21:35（請留意與學校一般表定abc堂的上課時間不同）。

cos_cname: 營業秘密與核心關鍵技術之保護
memo: 限科法所碩、專、博同學選修
cos_ename: Protecting Trade Secrets and Key Technology
dep_cname: 科技法律研究所碩士在職專班
crs_outline:
營業秘密作為關鍵的智慧財產權，在現代企業經營與競爭中扮演了重要角色。適當的保護不僅維護了產業倫理與競爭秩序，也是數位治理上的重要議題。因此，深入瞭解營業秘密法的規範結構、要件適用以及司法實踐，是必不可少的。在現今國際情勢下，為保護國家安全、產業競爭力與經濟發展，國家也需要保護其核心關鍵技術。對於國家核心關鍵技術的定義、決定與保護，對於國家安全與企業發展具有深遠的影響。國家安全法更進一步針對國家核心關鍵技術的營業秘密進行保護，使得國家安全法與營業秘密法的關係和交錯適用成為重要議題。另一方面，保護國家核心關鍵技術可能會對企業的營運與國際合作產生影響。因此，找到其間的平衡點是必須正視的議題。

本課程的目標是探討並理解營業秘密保護與國家核心關鍵技術保護的法制，並探討如何在企業需求與國家安全保護之間在實踐中找到平衡。學生將學習到這兩種保護策略的法律和政策基礎，以及如何影響企業營運和國家安全。

此外，本課程也將介紹出口管制的相關法律和規定。出口管制是一種政策工具，用於限制敏感技術或物品的出口，以維護國家安全和經濟競爭力。本課程將針對出口管制規範的要點、美國出口管制之規範與最新發展，以及我國出口管制規範與未來修正趨勢，加以說明。

本課程係由聯發科技股份有限公司副總經理暨法務長宿文堂老師、國立陽明交通大學林志潔特聘教授、陳在方所長共同講授。本課程的目標是使學生熟悉營業秘密保護、國家核心關鍵技術保護，以及出口管制的法律和政策。學生將學習到這些保護策略的理論基礎，並了解如何在實踐中應用。學生將深入學習與營業秘密相關的法律與理論，包括商業資訊保護的法制和實務，美國經濟間諜法，以及合理的保密措施與盡力防免責任。此外，學生也將探討與國家安全法和敏感資訊管制相關之規範。在出口管制部分，課程將介紹出口管制的基本概念，並深入研究以美國為主之出口管制的規範。課程也將涵蓋出口管制與國際貿易規範的關係，以及我國的出口管制規範。

dep_cname: 科技法律研究所碩士在職專班
costype: 領域課程-公民與倫理思考
crs_outline:
課程概述與目標：
隨著經濟富裕及國民壽命的延長，社會對醫療的質與量持續增加期待的同時，相關的法律爭議也層出不窮。由於醫療產業的特殊性，許多傳統公私法的市場及管制理論無法直接適用於醫事法律之爭議解決。基於醫療資源的有限性，醫事法律往往擺盪在多種相互衝突的目標之間，包括醫療品質、醫療成本、可近性。各國醫療法律制度之差異，反應了各國基於文化、歷史、社經條件等因素而對於這些價值的取捨。本課程旨在協助學生了解醫療產業的特性，明白許多法律規定多半是利益衝突下的權衡結果，建立面對具體個案時，運用跨學科知識與理論來理解及解決問題的能力。
本堂課將系統性介紹醫療糾紛的相關實務議題，並輔以實證法學的相關研究結果作為佐證。藉由討論醫療糾紛一系列的重要相關研究，由台灣醫療糾紛現狀出發、探討醫療過失的判斷、醫師的告知義務、醫療糾紛的民事及刑事責任、醫療糾紛的鑑定以及醫療糾紛的舉證責任等議題，幫助學生學習如何結合傳統的法學論述以及法實證分析研究，以提升其進行法學相關研究之基本能力。實證醫學與醫療糾紛之間的關係、以及臨床準則等相關議題。學生在本課程中，將學習關於醫療過失與醫療糾紛鑑定等重要議題，同時也將學習實證法學研究結果的掌握能力，對於將來從事相關實務工作或者研究的學生而言，是一堂不容錯過的課程。本課程將討論各國醫療糾紛改革方案，及台灣目前考慮中的選項。醫療機構法制的健全，勞動條件的改善，是台灣迫切的議題。接下來本課程將討論生命倫理議題，包括器官捐贈、安寧照護、生殖科技法學，以及臨床試驗倫理法制。本課程最後探討疫情蔓延時的公共衛生議題。
生醫產業可概括分為生物科技業及醫療業，科法學院的「生醫科技法律」及「醫療法律與政策」此二課程分別對應此二產業，為這兩大領域的入門課程。本課程係生醫產業經營與法律學分學程，以及生醫法律跨域學程的核心必修課程。學習者可透過本課程對此領域作最全面的了解，作為對個別子議題選修相關課程的基礎。

主要課程內容：
1、 醫療法律之基本原理原則
2、 醫病關係
3、 醫療組織
4、 生命倫理
5、 公共衛生
學習目標 :
1. 使同學掌握綜觀醫療政策與法律的理論與議題架構。
2. 對於重要的原理原則能有認識並知道如何操作。
3. 對於醫療政策與法律的基本議題能有清楚的認識。
4. 培養法學研究能力，能以醫療政策與法律的主題獨立研究。
預期學習成果 :
1. 同學們對於醫療政策與法律的知識系統架構能有清楚的掌握。
2. 對於醫療法的主要議題有基本的瞭解。
3. 能指出議題（issues）所在，瞭解相應的醫療法原理原則
4. 獨立完成研究，提出自己的見解

crs_outline:
主要課程內容：

本課程之目的在於介紹刑事訴訟法之各項程序，使同學充分瞭解刑事案件從偵查、審理、乃至定讞後非常救濟程序之過程。

本課程之特色有三：

一、刑事訴訟法涵蓋了刑事案件自偵查以來的案件進行程序，以及所有刑事程序參與者的角色分配及規範。刑事程序於實務上的操作尤為重要，因此本課程將以實務見解作為主軸，再視輔以學說上之見解。又近年來刑事訴訟法受到美國當事人進行主義影響甚深，本課程亦將納入比較法之觀點。

二、除了刑事訴訟法本文外，因刑事訴訟法的修正方向對於刑事案件的進行至關重要，故本課程亦將適時介紹國內外刑事程序之重大改革及修法議題。

三、本課程將納入實例解題，每堂課皆安排一定比例之時間，幫助同學熟悉國家考試考題型及走向。

學習目標：

一、熟悉刑事訴訟中各種程序之意義及在整體刑事訴訟程序上所扮演的角色。

二、辨認刑事訴訟中，學術與實務上的法律爭點。

三、接觸各種不同之國考題型，熟悉考試技巧。

上課方式：
實體教室、網路同步、網路非同步

crs_outline:
本課程為必修，修課同學必須就自己之獨立研究主題或碩士論文，以符合學術一般規範之方式，公開進行報告發表。修課同學與老師會針對報告內容予以評論、提問。目標為透過論文寫作之觀摩，練習論文之寫作與發表，提升對於議題的分析與掌握，培養對於學術報告之審閱與批評之能力。
主要課程內容:主要包含兩大部分
第一為對自己研究的進行，以及磨練口頭報告之技巧。第二部分則對於同學之報告提出回應與批評，以熟悉該領域之專業知識，並發展對議題之思考與評論之技巧。修課同學應認真聆聽報告並提出意見。除自己之報告主題外，會視修課情況，指定同學輪流擔任每與談人。與談人負有對當週報告主題提出評論之義務。
學習目標:
一、培養校級基本素養與核心能力：
＊資訊素養 
＊品德教育 
＊國際視野 
＊發現及解決問題的能力 
＊跨界多元思考的能力 
＊群己平衡的認知 
二、培養管理學院學生基本素養與核心能力：
＊發掘、分析管理相關領域問題、尋求解決答案並進行決策的能力 
三、培養科法碩學生基本素養與核心能力：
＊建立從事法律實務工作應具備的法學專業素養、國際觀與倫理思維 
＊培養對社會時事發展的觀察與分析能力 
＊發現及解決問題的能力 
＊科際間知識的整合以及實證研究方法　
預期學習成果:
若上述學習目標能力皆能具備當然最好，但在完成本課程後，學生最應該具備發表學術研究之能力、在學術會議發表之能力以及對學術作品進行思考與批判之能力。

dep_cname: 科技法律研究所碩士在職專班
crs_outline:
請注意，本課程為密集式上課Fast-track課程，每次三小時，上課時間為：上課時間為：9/12(六)、9/19(六)、9/20(日)、10/3(六)、10/4(日)、10/17(六)、10/31(六)、11/7(六)、11/8(日)、11/14(六)、11/21(六)期末考(2小時)，都是上午14:20-17:20上課。

八里雙屍命案、乙醚殺妻案、國道陸客團遊覽車縱火案及Trans-Colorado Airlines Flight 2286等案均因法醫毒物鑑定報告而走向不同的偵查方向，進而釐清事實真相。多數死因不明的案件，通常會透過毒物化學鑑定來確認或排除是否有毒藥物的影響，然而，與廣為人知的DNA鑑定不同，法醫毒物鑑定雖然應用極廣，但是清楚實務內涵的人並不多見；同時，「Forensic」具有涉及法律或應用在法庭上的意義，因此，本課程欲結合法醫毒物案例分析與相關法律議題，進而探討新聞中常看到的相關爭議，特別著重在酒駕案件及濫用藥物的部分。此外，涉及鑑識科學的一環，鑑定報告的法律效力、鑑定的偏誤及迷思也會一併探討。透過以上授課內容，希望可以藉此門課初步認識鑑識科學在法律上的地位與其真正的意義。

本課程之特色：
一、認識法醫毒物學，並且了解在實務上的應用及限制。
二、建立對鑑識科學的基本概念。
三、鑑定在法庭上的地位與探討。

學習目標：
一、了解法醫毒物學的基本內涵。
二、破除鑑定迷思。
三、學習如何進行不同學門間的對話。

dep_cname: 科技法律研究所碩士在職專班
crs_outline:
本課程之目的在於提供學員一個全面性之專利制度概念、知識與處理技能，並以美國及台灣之實務運作為解說及討論之重點。專利法制之發展與科技研發，產業競爭及企業經營，有著密切的關連；法條之內容與實務在近二十年來產生了快速的變革，加上美國專利實務引領全球相關制度之發展，因此本課程結合「產業競爭」之背景及「實證研究」之成果，以解說美國專利案例為主，並據以實證分析我國智財法院成立以來的專利判決，同時也對新興的專利市場及專利事業體(NPEs: Non-Practicing Entities或PAEs: Patent Assertion Entities)在開放式創新(Open Innovation)架構下的發展與經營模式(Business Model)，提供科技、產業與法律整合的觀念與運作知識。除了電子與資訊科技專利外，醫藥專利涉及食品醫藥管制與價格競爭，本課程特別安排講授美國生醫專利相關課題。本課程重點為：(1)專利要件、申請策略與說明書解讀；(2)專利侵害判斷及迴避設計；(3)專利訴訟及行政程序；(4)無形資產評價、專利及營業秘密損害賠償；(5)專利授權及競爭法之限制；以及(6)專利布局及智財戰略。個別主題之內容，皆涵蓋案例解說及經營管理之策略性思維與作為。

學習目標：
1. 本課程之目的在於提供學員一個全面性之專利制度概念與知識，並以美國及台灣之實務運作為解說及討論之重點，兼談中國大陸之現況。
2. 本課程結合「產業競爭」之背景以及「實證研究」之成果，以解說美國專利案例為主進行教學。

cos_ename: The Re-conceptualization of National Security in International Economic Law
dep_cname: 科技法律研究所碩士在職專班
crs_outline:
The laws governing global investment and trade ("international economic law") are largely controlled by agreements between nations (e.g., BITs, WTO rules). These international investment and trade agreements set forth the conditions which govern the relationship and contain exceptions which allow nations to "override" the states' contractual obligations. Among the most significant exception is the "national security" or "essential security" exception which permits sovereigns to take measures ostensibly violating the contract but justifiable based on the need to defend security.

Of course, the key question is whether the state acted legitimately and not for impermissible reasons such as protectionism simply using security as a justification.

In recent years, an increasing array of measures have been enacted globally including tariffs, inbound/outbound screening, and export controls based on alleged national security threats. The proximate cause is attributable to the China-U.S. hegemonic rivalry, and can also be linked to increasing economic nationalism, concern over resilience, and endeavors to re-industrialize economies.

The issue will take on increasing significance as targets of governmental measures are increasingly filing claims in international tribunals alleging violations of agreements or WTO rules (and filing claims in domestic courts as well although we will focus mostly on the international investment and trade context until the last class).

Are such measures justified by legitimate security threats or do the measures constitute prohibited protectionism? The definition, conceptualization, and contours of national security will control the answer.

Students will explore the changing conceptualization of security from the more traditional armed conflict and defense of territorial integrity to a more expansive conceptualization encompassing not merely military strength but also economic, technological, and ideological power...

Learning Outcomes

By the end of the course, students will:

have a firm understanding of the current global economic governance architecture;
learn about the classic and new re-conceptualization of national security;
explore separating measures into defensive and offensive deployments;
discuss the perils of unfettered expansion of national security's definition; and
explore emerging issues connected to the topic.

Due to the space limitations of the NYCU course syllabus format, please refer to the instructor's complete Course Syllabus for detailed course descriptions, readings, assignments, and assessment requirements.

memo: 授課教師︰邱仕謙
cos_ename: Innovation and  Information Security Management in Corporate Governance Practices
dep_cname: 科技法律研究所碩士在職專班
crs_outline:
課程目標﹕
本課程從公司治理視角出發，解析ISO 56001（創新管理）與ISO 27001（資訊安全）兩系統在企業創新流程中的協同角色。透過案例實作，引導學員建構可落實、可評量及可持續改進，且能有效運用資訊安全管理工具的創新管理流程，確保符合公司治理與法規遵循要求。
課程說明﹕
近年來，營業秘密洩密案件頻傳，顯示企業長期以來僅倚賴智慧財產權來保護創新成果，卻忽視資訊安全管理的被動思維，已難以有效保護企業研發成果，對企業永續經營構成不可忽視的風險與挑戰。
符合公司治理要求的創新管理系統，不應局限於創新成果的管理與運用。更要從創新策略、環境變化、風險控管及利害關係人等多元視角，並有效運用資訊安全管理工具，全面審視創新流程的每一個環節，來確保創新成果的經濟利益。
為此，金管會將「創新管理系統」及「資通安全風險管理」納入上市櫃公司ESG評鑑指標。企業當應運用這兩個系統的協同運作，強化創新的源頭到創新成果的運用的流程管理，以強化公司治理的整體韌性。
本課程以創新管理系統為主體(兼含TIPS與ISO 56001)，並整合資訊安全管理(ISO 27001)管理架構。結合實務案例探討與實作，學員將不僅深入理解創新管理的制度設計原理，更能掌握系統面臨資訊安全風險下的風險控制思維，建立兼具公司治理與法規遵循要求的創新管理系統。
